contract.settlement_definition: Each period contract settles only on goals scored in that 20-minute period: KXNHL1P/2P/3P are three-way style markets (a team wins the period, or the 'period tie' contract pays YES if neither team wins), KXNHL*PSPREAD pays YES if the named team wins the period by more than the floor_strike (1.5 or 2.5, i.e. a two- or three-goal margin), KXNHL*PTOTAL pays YES if the teams collectively score more than the strike in that period (for example 2.5 or 3.5), and KXNHL1PBTTS (title only, no rules text) covers both teams scoring in the first period. Rules text is recovered for the nine 1P/2P/3P winner, spread and total series; each says only goals scored during that period count. Third-period contracts exclude overtime. Postponed games stay open if begun within 48h, otherwise resolve to a fair price.

rules_evidence.quote: If neither team wins the 1st period of the Pittsburgh vs Anaheim NHL game
rules_evidence.establishes: The period winner series includes an explicit tie contract: YES if neither team wins the period, so ties are a priced outcome with a separate contract rather than a push.

rules_evidence.quote: Only goals scored during the 3rd period (excluding overtime) of play count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Third-period markets stop at 60:00: overtime goals never count, but empty-net goals in the third period do.

rules_evidence.quote: If the teams collectively score more than 3.5 goals in the 1st Period of the St. Louis vs Nashville NHL game
rules_evidence.establishes: Period total rungs are one-sided 'more than x.5' contracts, with high rungs like 3.5 that are rare first-period events, and the strike scale differs by period.

rules_evidence.quote: If Pittsburgh wins by more than 1.5 goals in the 1st period of the Pittsburgh vs Anaheim NHL game
rules_evidence.establishes: Period spread is a margin of two or more goals within 20 minutes, a rare event that depends on cross-team dispersion, not on mean difference alone.

rules_evidence.quote: Only goals scored during the 2nd period of play count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Second-period winner/tie markets ignore the entering score: the target is the period-two goal difference only, a mixture over the score state carried in from period one.

rules_evidence.quote: If the teams collectively score more than 2.5 goals in the 3rd Period
rules_evidence.establishes: Third-period totals are one-sided 'more than x.5' rungs counted on the 40:00-60:00 window, which includes late empty-net goals but (per the note) not overtime.

rules_evidence.quote: wins by more than 1.5 goals in the 3rd period (excluding overtime)
rules_evidence.establishes: Third-period spread excludes OT explicitly, so a regulation-tied game contributes only its 3rd-period margin and empty-net goals in that period push margins to 2+.

variants_and_edge_cases: Copy-paste note: the 1st and 2nd period rules texts repeat 'Note: 3rd period markets do not include overtime', which is irrelevant to those periods but shows rules are templated; the 3rd period series is the only one where overtime exclusion matters.

Period tie markets versus team-win markets: a three-outcome family priced as separate binaries, so the three probabilities must sum to one up to fees and the tie mass is the key quantity at a mean of about one goal per team.
KXNHL1PBTTS is the only period series without rules text (TITLE_ONLY): whether it needs a goal credited to each team in the first period, and own-goal handling, are unseen.

Penalty and period boundaries: a power play that starts late in a period carries into the next period but goals count in the period in which they are scored; no strike construction exists for end-of-period carryover.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official NHL period-by-period scoring in the game summary; Kalshi resolves from league scoring by period.

mechanism.summary: A period is a 20-minute slice of the same scoring process with its own rates and its own state. Goals per team per period have a mean near one, so outcomes are dominated by 0, 1 and 2 goals: P(period tie) is large and the winner markets are mostly questions about how much mass sits on 0-0 and 1-1. Rates differ by period: the first is shaped by opening deployment and fresh goalies; the second has the long change that tends to lift scoring; the third is dominated by score effects and, at the end, goalie pulls and empty-net goals. Because later periods start from a random score state, period two and three markets are mixtures over entering margin. A single power play can decide a period, so penalty timing and counts are a concentrated volatility source, and referees may balance calls within a game.

stages.name: Period-specific scoring rate for each team
stages.description: Team goal rate per period is the season rate times a period factor: first-period rates are usually the lowest, the second period benefits from the long change that makes defensive-zone line changes hard, and the third responds to score. Team-specific period tendencies (slow starters, second-period scorers) exist but are noisy over 60-80 games. Opposing goalie and the pairing of attack with the defence set the level for each team separately.
stages.distribution: Poisson-gamma goal counts per team with mean about 0.9-1.1 per period; period effects of order 5-15 percent on the mean, team period effects smaller and heavily shrunk.

stages.name: Lineup, goalie and coach deployment inside the period
stages.description: Starting goalie quality and who is on the ice in the first minutes shape period one, while coaches adjust line matching and ice time by period and score. A goalie pulled mid-game changes the second and third periods for that team, and a skater injured in period one changes the rest of the game. Deployment effects are small per period but unlike full-game markets they operate on a short sample where a few shifts matter. Rest and back-to-back status enter here through the backup-goalie probability for period one and a possible late-game fade.
stages.distribution: Discrete lineup states with continuous deployment shifts; mixture over goalie identity before confirmation.

stages.name: Entering score state and late-period control
stages.description: For periods two and three the game starts from a random margin drawn from the earlier periods, so the market is a mixture over entering states; leaders reduce risk, trailers press, and in the last two minutes of the third the trailing team pulls its goalie, adding both an equalizer chance and an empty-net chance in the same period. The third period includes empty-net goals but excludes OT, making its totals fatter than the first two with a larger share of one-sided late goals.
stages.distribution: Mixture over entering margin {-2,...,+2} with state-dependent rates; third-period end process with jump component from pulls.

stages.name: Power plays, penalty timing and referee balancing
stages.description: Power-play minutes are rare and lumpy within a period: zero, one or two minor penalties, with a single PP converting roughly a fifth of the time and lifting that period's goals by a large factor. Referees may even out calls within a game, so the number of penalties in later periods depends on the earlier imbalance. The penalty process interacts with team special-teams quality and with unit deployment.
stages.distribution: Compound count: Poisson penalties per period times conversion Bernoulli, which concentrates heavy-tail mass; counts overdispersed by crew and game state.

stages.name: Joint count model and settlement of the three-way market
stages.description: The market pays on tie, home win or away win in the period, or on the margin or total thresholds. The probabilities come from a bivariate count model with period-specific variance and correlation, and cross-period dependence through score state and game total; the tie probability is the diagonal and is large. The 3rd-period exclusion of overtime must be encoded, and the period markets are NOT independent of one another or of the final result: the periods compose the final score, so cross-period dependence through score state is part of the joint model. The first-period BTTS contract is the off-diagonal-free mass P(H1>=1, A1>=1) of the same period-one bivariate model, so its price is driven by the two teams' first-period rates and their correlation.
stages.distribution: Bivariate overdispersed counts with period-specific zero mass; P(0-0) is about 12-16 percent and P(tie) in the low-to-mid 30s percent range (the Poisson(1,1) benchmark is about 31 percent, overdispersion raises it slightly; both unsourced and to be measured).

environment.note: Rinks are indoors, so weather is irrelevant, but the home flag and last-change edge are team-versus-team effects that differ by period; carried by nhl.period_home_ice_split.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and back-to-back status change who is in goal in period one and possibly late-game fade; stakes are negligible in November and are not claimed.

nhl.period_entry_state_matrix.label: Entering-period score-state distribution and state-conditional rates
nhl.period_entry_state_matrix.mechanism: pmf of the score margin entering periods two and three together with team rates conditional on margin.
nhl.period_entry_state_matrix.rationale: The pregame win probability does not give the distribution of the margin at 20:00 and 40:00, and period-three scoring depends on that margin through score effects. Markets for later periods are mixtures that cannot be priced from unconditional period rates.
nhl.period_entry_state_matrix.measurement: From period-by-period history compute for each team the empirical transition matrix of margin after one and two periods, shrunk to a model-based matrix from the bivariate period count model (prior strength 30 games); compute rates of goals and SOG for and against per period conditional on entering margin in {-2,-1,0,+1,+2 or more} with k=40 team-period minutes shrinkage; output the expected rate in period p as a mixture sum over margins of P(margin) x rate(margin). Include the effect of pulled goalie probability in period 3.
free_sources: Natural Stat Trick score state splits
raw_data: goals and shots by period with running score
nhl.period_entry_state_matrix.why: Provides the entering-state mixture that period 2 and 3 winner, spread and total contracts require.

nhl.third_period_equalizer_hazard.label: Late-game equalizer and empty-net hazard by team and coach
nhl.third_period_equalizer_hazard.mechanism: Converts a one-goal late deficit into tie or two-goal-loss outcomes using 6v5 rates and the coach's pull time.
nhl.third_period_equalizer_hazard.rationale: The existing empty_net input is a single bucket for 'pulled-goalie timing'; for tie probability the two competing outcomes of a pull (equalizer vs empty-net goal against) and their dependence on pull time are what move the diagonal of the score distribution. Pull time has drifted earlier league-wide and differs by coach.
nhl.third_period_equalizer_hazard.measurement: From play-by-play, for every regular-season and playoff game since 2015-16 find states with the trailing team down exactly one goal and the goalie pulled; per team-coach compute (a) median pull time in seconds remaining, (b) equalizer rate = goals for per 60 minutes of 6v5 time, (c) empty-net goals against per 60 of 6v5 time. Shrink each to league with k=20 pulls, weight seasons with 2-year half-life, and reset on a coaching change. Output pregame P(equalizer | trailing by 1 at T-3:00) and P(EN | trailing by 1) per team pair.
free_sources: NHL API play-by-play (situationCode and event times)
raw_data: play-by-play events: period, clock, strength situationCode, goalie-in-net flag, goal events
coach by game
nhl.third_period_equalizer_hazard.why: In the third-period contracts empty-net goals count and overtime does not, so the pull and equalizer rates directly set the last two minutes' goals for both totals and spreads.

nhl.period_penalty_intensity_balance.label: Period-level penalty intensity and within-game balancing
nhl.period_penalty_intensity_balance.mechanism: Distribution of the number of minors per period and the tendency to even out calls against the earlier imbalance.
nhl.period_penalty_intensity_balance.rationale: Because one power play can decide a 20-minute period, the count distribution and its dependence on earlier calls matter more here than in full-game markets. Referee balancing is a mechanism where penalties against a team become less likely after the opponent has received more.
nhl.period_penalty_intensity_balance.measurement: From play-by-play compute for each period the pmf of minors called on each team; estimate a logit/Poisson regression of the next penalty on cumulative penalty differential with period fixed effects, using crew effects as random intercept with prior sd 0.1; shrink team taken/drawn rates with k=300 minutes. Forecast per period: expected minors for each side as a function of crew, teams and period; simulate balancing within the game for periods two and three.
raw_data: penalty events with period, minute, team, referee crew
nhl.period_penalty_intensity_balance.why: Concentrated volatility source for short windows; also tests whether early imbalances change later-period tie mass.

nhl.period_pair_count_model.label: Period-level bivariate count model with cross-period dependence
nhl.period_pair_count_model.mechanism: Joint pmf of the two teams' goals in a period with period-specific dispersion, correlation and zero mass.
nhl.period_pair_count_model.rationale: The full-game dispersion parameter cannot be reused for a 20-minute window where zero mass and tie probability are driven by different variances; moreover periods within a game are dependent through game total and score effects.
nhl.period_pair_count_model.measurement: Fit a bivariate negative-binomial or Poisson-mixture model with parameters (mu_home, mu_away, dispersion, correlation) per period index using all games since 2010-11, with covariates team strength and PP expectations; estimate cross-period dependence by a shared game random effect (variance parameter) and a score-effect term; validate on frequency of 0-0, ties and margins of two or more in each period; recalibrate each season.
raw_data: goals by team and period for every game
nhl.period_pair_count_model.why: Gives the tie, winner, spread and total functionals in one coherent distribution so period contracts agree with each other.

nhl.ratings_script_distribution.label: Ratings-only pregame score-path distribution (lead/trail/tied time shares and entering-state matrix)
nhl.ratings_script_distribution.mechanism: Simulated from team goal rates alone, the distribution of score states by period and the share of 60 minutes spent leading, trailing or tied shapes shot volume, star deployment, pull timing and empty-net goals without ever touching a price.
nhl.ratings_script_distribution.rationale: The catalog nhl.game_script_prob derives its win probability from ratings AND the market line, so it is contaminated by the benchmark. This replacement is built only from market-free inputs: it keeps the useful scenario-probability content (conditional state mixtures, not a single win probability) while leaving the market line as a comparison target. The subtle point is that the object needed is a distribution over states, not one number.
nhl.ratings_script_distribution.measurement: For each team, set expected 5v5 and special-teams goal rates for the game as lambda_i = league mean x (attack_i x defence_j adjusted xG ratings, shrunk with prior_to_current_blend where available, or ratings built from score-adjusted xGF/xGA per 60 over a 40-game EWMA with 20-game half-life shrunk 25 games toward league mean) x goalie factor (confirmed or probability-weighted starter GSAx per 60 shrunk 1000 shots) plus a home-ice constant estimated from the last 5 seasons. Simulate 20000 games with a negative-binomial goal process with the fitted dispersion, event times drawn from a time-varying rate with score effects, a pull rule at the coach-specific trailing time, and OT 3v3 play. Output per game: P(lead/tied/trail) entering each period, expected minutes in each score state, P(margin>=2 entering the third), and expected 6v5 minutes per team. As-of timestamp: latest ratings and confirmed or probabilistic starter before puck drop; never include any sportsbook or Kalshi price.
free_sources: Natural Stat Trick team game logs
NHL API play-by-play for pull times (api-web.nhle.com)
raw_data: team-game 5v5 and special-teams xGF/xGA per 60 with score and venue splits
goalie GSAx by game and shots faced
coach-specific goalie-pull times from play-by-play
period-by-period score history per game
nhl.ratings_script_distribution.why: Gives the contract a market-free script latent (state mixture and entering-state matrix) so that benchmark prices remain an independent yardstick.

nhl.period_home_ice_split.label: Home-ice and last-change effect by period (home flag, period-specific home goal share)
nhl.period_home_ice_split.mechanism: The home team gets last change at every stoppage and the home crowd and scorer effects are modest and constant in size, but their effect on a 20-minute winner or spread contract differs by period because deployment, score state and the second-period long change interact with the home bench position.
nhl.period_home_ice_split.rationale: Period winner and spread contracts are team-versus-team, so a small constant home edge shifts every tie, win and rung probability and is not captured by team ratings alone. A single full-game home constant mis-scales the period effect: it is most visible in match-ups of the first period when coaches can pick the matchup, and it is compressed in the third by score effects. Reviewers noted no home input existed in this record.
nhl.period_home_ice_split.measurement: From team-period goal and xG data since 2015-16 fit goal differential per period = team strength difference + home indicator x period (three coefficients) with season fixed effects; shrink each period coefficient toward the pooled home edge with a prior of 25 percent of the pooled value variance, estimate on 5v5 xG and on goals separately, and refresh yearly. Treat last-change strength as a league-level effect only (no team-specific estimate, samples are too small). As-of: all games before the target date.
raw_data: team-game period scores and period xG with home/away flag
score and strength state by period
nhl.period_home_ice_split.why: Supplies the missing home flag and period-specific home edge to winner, spread and tie contracts of each of the three periods.

nhl.rest_fatigue_period_profile.label: Rest and back-to-back fatigue profile by period (and its backup-goalie channel)
nhl.rest_fatigue_period_profile.mechanism: A team on the second night of a back-to-back or after long travel plays a higher share of games with a backup goalie, which changes the first-period goal rate, and may fade late in the game, so the rest effect is not constant across periods.
nhl.rest_fatigue_period_profile.rationale: Reviewers argued rest was ignored because the record treated it as a full-game constant. The channel that is certain is goalie identity (backup starts concentrate on back-to-backs), which hits period one; the possible skater fatigue channel would show up as a later-period fade and is unproven. The input keeps the two channels separate so that the certain one is not diluted by the uncertain one.
nhl.rest_fatigue_period_profile.measurement: For every team-game since 2015-16 compute rest days, back-to-back second-night flag and time-zone miles travelled; regress period goal differential and period xG differential on rest differential interacted with period (3 coefficients), with team strength and home controls and season fixed effects. Add the backup-start probability from the goalie start forecast as a separate covariate so the fatigue term is estimated net of goalie identity. Shrink period coefficients to the pooled rest effect with a prior sd of one third of the pooled estimate. As-of: schedule is known weeks ahead, goalie confirmation arrives on game day.
free_sources: NHL boxscores for goalie of record
raw_data: team schedule with dates and venues
goalie of record per game and period xG/goals by team-period
nhl.rest_fatigue_period_profile.why: Adds period-specific rest effects, especially the first-period backup-goalie channel, that a full-game rest constant would blur.

nhl.period_split.reason: The right object but needs to be a period-specific rate multiplier by team shrunk to league, not a raw list of period shares, which are noisy over a season.

nhl.xg_for.reason: Provides the base chance-quality rate per 60 that is scaled to 20 minutes with period factors.

nhl.xg_against.reason: Defensive base rate for the opposing team's period scoring; strength-split so PP time can be removed.

nhl.pace.reason: Attempt volume is secondary because goals per period depend more on conversion and power plays than on small differences in attempts.

nhl.goalie_start.reason: Affects both teams' goals; the confirmed goalie matters in the first period (fresh) and for pulls later.

nhl.special_teams.reason: One power play can swing a period, but special-team talent is only persistent modestly, so its effect is on tails.

nhl.penalty_rates.reason: Sets PP counts per period; needs to be refined with period-specific and balancing terms from the new penalty input.

nhl.score_state.reason: Score effects are central to period three and to second-period rates after a lead; in-game state, so only expectation is pregame. The catalog measurement integrates score-state rates over 'pregame win probability and total'; that must be the ratings-only nhl.ratings_script_distribution, not a market-implied win probability or total.

nhl.game_script_prob.reason: Catalog measurement uses the market line, so it is market-contaminated, and a single win probability is not the entering-margin distribution this contract needs. Replaced by nhl.period_entry_state_matrix (state matrix) and the market-free nhl.ratings_script_distribution.

nhl.empty_net.reason: Third-period totals, spreads and ties all depend on EN goals and pulls; mislabelled secondary.

nhl.long_change_effect.reason: Plausible league-wide second-period effect but team-specific versions are noisy; keep as a league-level multiplier, not a team feature.

nhl.opening_shift_deployment.reason: The first shift is under a minute of a 20-minute period; its information about the full-period outcome is negligible once goalie and top lines are known. Removed from stage s2, role_personnel coverage and interaction 4; the first-shift line is not a driver.

nhl.coach_deployment_style.reason: Coach line-matching and PP time allocation may influence scoring, but the effect is hard to isolate per period and acts through already modelled rates.

nhl.total_goal_dispersion.reason: Full-game dispersion does not apply to a 20-minute window with different zero mass; replace by the period-level bivariate model. Not claimed in any stage or coverage; replaced by nhl.period_pair_count_model.

m.rules_text.reason: Third-period OT exclusion, tie contract and goal-only counting define the target; the rules notes are templated across periods.

nhl.pdo_regression.reason: Luck regression is slow-moving and period results are too noisy for it to matter; it is already inside team ratings.

interactions.mechanism: Third period outcomes depend on the margin entering the period: with a one-goal lead the leader sits and the trailer eventually pulls, giving a late burst of goals; with a tie there is no pull until near the end, so the same ratings imply different totals and winner probabilities by entering state.
interactions.how_to_test: Split third-period goals by entering margin and compare scoring rate and EN share against a margin-free model.

interactions.mechanism: Period tie probability is the diagonal of a bivariate count whose total is small, so a shift in total changes tie mass more than a shift in difference; tie, win and spread markets must be priced from the same joint, not marginals.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised period tie rate by bin of expected team means with the product-of-marginals prediction.

interactions.mechanism: Hypothesis only: the second-period long change makes defensive-zone line changes harder, so teams that concentrate ice time in top lines may gain or lose more than teams that roll four lines; any effect is conditional on deployment and may be zero.
interactions.how_to_test: Named contrast: the second-period minus first/third-period goal-differential gap for the top versus bottom tercile of teams ranked by forward TOI concentration; reject if the gap difference is within noise across seasons.

interactions.mechanism: One extra power play lifts the period's expected goals by a fifth to a quarter of a goal, and the effect is convex because a second PP can follow a goal in the same period; the penalty count distribution and PP efficiency multiply, so uncertain counts fatten the upper tail.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin periods by number of minors called and compute realised goals and tie rate relative to the zero-PP baseline.

interactions.mechanism: First-period chances against a backup goalie depend on his pregame workload and on the opponent chance quality; the interaction is confined to period one, before score state and line matching dominate, and should not be carried to periods two and three.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare first-period goals against for backups versus starters at fixed opponent xG per 60, and confirm no such gap in periods two and three.

nonlinearities.shape: Zero-heavy count: P(0) falls exponentially in the mean
nonlinearities.why: At a mean near one goal per team the probability of 0-0 and of ties changes quickly with small rate shifts, so a linear approximation in period goal rate mis-prices tie contracts near the mean.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold in the last two minutes of the third period
nonlinearities.why: Pulled goalies occur almost only in the last 2:00 of the third period; goals scored in that window are a different process, so third-period totals have a thick tail not shared by the first two periods.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in the number of power plays in the period
nonlinearities.why: Each added power play raises goal expectation by a fixed increment and increases the chance of a multi-goal period more than proportionally, so period totals above 2.5 depend on the upper tail of the penalty distribution.

contract.settlement_definition: KXNHLGOAL, KXNHLAST and KXNHLPTS are ladders of 'N+' contracts (sampled strikes: 1.5 on assists, 2.5 on goals and points; the 0.5 rung is inferred, not seen) that pay YES if the named skater records at least that many in the listed game; if the player is active but never enters the game the market settles to the last fair market price before game start, and once he enters it settles on the stat recorded. KXNHLFIRSTGOAL pays if the named player scores the first goal of the game (regulation or overtime, shootout goals excluded) with a separate No Goalscorer market. KXNHLANYGOAL is title-only. None of the ladder texts says whether overtime or empty-net goals count; official box-score credit is assumed.

rules_evidence.quote: If a player is active but never enters the game, the market settles to the last fair market price before game start.
rules_evidence.establishes: The text covers a player who is "active" but never enters: such a player settles at the last fair market price before game start. It does not define "active", nor say how a healthy scratch or pregame-out skater resolves, so that case is unverified (pp5).

rules_evidence.quote: Shootout goals do not count.
rules_evidence.establishes: First-goal scoring covers regulation and overtime goals only; a game decided only by shootout resolves No Goalscorer, so P(no goal) is a real outcome.

rules_evidence.quote: Once a player enters the game, the market settles based on the player's goals recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: Goal ladders settle on the official goals credited to the skater once he enters, so post-game scoring changes and own-goal attribution flow into settlement; OT inclusion is not stated.

variants_and_edge_cases: Ladder nesting: 1+, 2+, 3+ rungs on goals, assists and points are nested events; points rungs also nest goals and assists (points >= goals), so rung probabilities for one player must be mutually consistent.
KXNHLANYGOAL is title-only (no markets listed): whether empty-net and overtime goals count, and how the market differs from the N+ ladder, is unseen and marked CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.

Reconciled series: KXNHLF10G (either-team early goal) moved to game_events and KXNHLSEASONPPTS (season points) to the season-counting archetype; the single-game skater chain here no longer carries them.
Official scoring credit can be revised after the game (assists, goal attribution), so the data version used for settlement matters; the sampled text does not say which feed is authoritative.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official NHL box score and play-by-play game summary for goals, assists and points; season totals from official NHL stats.

mechanism.summary: A skater's goals, assists and points in a game are counts accumulated only while he is on the ice and credited by the scorer. First, availability and role decide whether he plays and where: line, power-play unit, penalty kill. Second, minutes by strength state set the number of opportunities, with power-play time the most valuable and the most uncertain because it depends on penalties called. Third, goals follow from shots times shot quality times finishing against the opposing goalie, with P(at least one) saturating as the mean grows. Fourth, assists and points depend on how often the player is credited on goals his team scores while he is on the ice (individual points percentage), which depends on role: forwards on scoring lines have high shares, defencemen lower. Fifth, the team's goal environment scales everything, so multi-point rungs are driven by team total and by whether the star is on the ice for several of them.

stages.name: Availability, lineup slot and replacement redistribution
stages.description: Whether the skater plays and in which slot is the first stage: a healthy scratch or injury settles at the last fair price if he is active but never enters, while teammates' absences promote players to the top line or the first power-play unit. A player's ceiling in the game depends on who replaces whom, and promotions are partially known from morning skate and partially only at warmups. The replacement pattern determines minutes and linemates, so it propagates into every later stage.
stages.distribution: Discrete lineup scenarios per team; each scenario sets a TOI and unit assignment with different means.

stages.name: Time on ice and power-play volume
stages.description: Minutes are split into even strength, power play and penalty kill, and roughly a third of a top forward's scoring comes on the power play in few minutes. PP minutes depend on the number of penalties the opponent takes (random) and on the unit's share of each power play, which is front-loaded because a minor ends on a goal. Blowouts compress the stars' minutes and late-game extra-attacker deployment adds a small block of minutes to specific players.
stages.distribution: Minutes: roughly normal at even strength with sd of 2-3 minutes; PP minutes compound (Poisson penalties times unit share) with heavy right tail.

stages.name: Shot generation, shot quality and finishing for goals
stages.description: Goals per game follow from shot attempts, on-target share, location quality and the skater's finishing, against the opposing starting goalie. The individual expected-goals rate per 60 is the most stable baseline; finishing talent varies and is shrunk hard. P(at least one goal) = 1 - exp(-lambda) saturates, so a doubling of the mean does not double the probability, while the 2+ and 3+ rungs depend on the tail of a count with lambda of 0.3-0.5 for top scorers. The skater shot volume enters explicitly through nhl.shot_rate (shot attempts and shots on goal per 60 by state), not only implicitly through ixG.
stages.distribution: Poisson or zero-inflated count of goals with lambda about 0.1-0.5; P(2+) about an order of magnitude below P(1+).

stages.name: Assist and point credit on team goals
stages.description: Points are credited on goals scored while the player is on the ice: a team goal gives a point to the scorer and up to two assists, and the individual points percentage (his points divided by on-ice goals for) is a stable role-dependent share. Expected points = on-ice goal exposure x IPP, where the exposure combines team quality on the ice and linemate finishing, and secondary assists are noisy. This makes assists and points more dependent on teammates than goals, and correlates assists with the team's goal environment.
stages.distribution: Credit structure: each goal yields 1 goal + 0-2 assists (about 12-15 percent unassisted); assists/points are compound counts with higher correlation to team goals than individual goals.

stages.name: Team goal environment and special settlement variants
stages.description: The team's goals scored scale every skater-level count: a team with an expected three goals gives its top line roughly 3x more chances for a multi-point night than a team with two, and game total and script (blowout, empty-net) correlate players across a team. KXNHLFIRSTGOAL is different in kind: a competing-risk race in which the player's share of his team's goal hazard times P(his team scores first) gives his probability, with a separate 'No Goalscorer' outcome when regulation and overtime are scoreless (shootout goals excluded); KXNHLANYGOAL is the 1+ rung of the goal chain.
stages.distribution: Team goals ~ NB with mean 2.6-3.4; first-goal timing roughly exponential with mean 12-14 minutes; season total approximately normal with games-remaining variance.

environment.note: A skater's single-game goal and assist counts are not affected by weather or altitude in an indoor rink; rink scoring and recording factors act through team rates, which are captured by the opposing team and goalie inputs.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach effects on skater production act through TOI, PP unit assignment and line combinations, which are modelled directly as role inputs; no separate coach-level feature adds information beyond those slots for single-game ladders.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and standings stakes affect whether stars play, which is captured by availability and next-man-up inputs; the residual effect on per-minute production of a skater who plays is negligible.

nhl.ipp_by_state.label: Individual points percentage by strength state (points per on-ice goal for)
nhl.ipp_by_state.mechanism: Share of team goals scored while on ice on which the player is credited with a goal or assist.
nhl.ipp_by_state.rationale: Points are credited on team goals, so expected points equal on-ice goals for times the share of those on which the skater is credited; this share is far more stable than assists per game and is role dependent (forwards on scoring lines high, defencemen lower, PP1 shooters very high).
nhl.ipp_by_state.measurement: For each skater and strength state (EV, PP) compute IPP = (goals + assists) / on-ice goals for, using 3 seasons weighted by 0.5/0.3/0.2 and shrunk to position-and-role priors with k=25 on-ice goals; separate primary and secondary assist components, shrinking secondary toward position mean with k=60; apply per-60 conversion: expected points per game = sum over states of (on-ice GF/60 x state TOI/60 x IPP_state).
free_sources: NHL API play-by-play (goals with scorer and assists, on-ice players)
raw_data: goal events with scorer, assist1, assist2, on-ice skaters by strength state
nhl.ipp_by_state.why: Provides the stable credit share that converts team scoring into points and assists; absent from the draft which relied on raw assist rate and finishing.

nhl.onice_xgf_per60.label: On-ice expected goals for per 60 by strength state (RAPM-adjusted)
nhl.onice_xgf_per60.mechanism: Team scoring chances created while the player is on ice, adjusted for teammates, opponents and zone starts.
nhl.onice_xgf_per60.rationale: Individual xG measures only the shooter's own attempts but points depend on all chances the player's line creates; a forward on a top line has points even when he does not shoot much. Linemate_quality is a single-label proxy; a regularised on-ice xGF rate is the measurable form.
nhl.onice_xgf_per60.measurement: Estimate per-skater on-ice xGF per 60 at 5v5 and on the PP with ridge regression on shift data (3-season window, half-life 1.5 seasons, shrink toward position mean with prior sd chosen by cross-validation) controlling for teammates, opponents, zone starts and score state. Projected on-ice xGF for the game uses projected linemates (from lines input) and is multiplied by the opposing team's defence factor and the opposing goalie factor.
raw_data: shift-level on-ice player sets with xG events
nhl.onice_xgf_per60.why: Linemate and role effects on points and assists enter the model as a measurable on-ice chance-creation rate.

nhl.first_goal_scorer_share.label: First-goal scorer share and team first-goal probability
nhl.first_goal_scorer_share.mechanism: Probability that the player scores the game's first goal given team-level first-goal race and his share within the scoring line.
nhl.first_goal_scorer_share.rationale: The first-goalscorer contract is a competing-risk race: either team scores first, and given that the scorer is drawn from the players on ice at that moment weighted by shot share. Early-game deployment and early power plays raise top-line and PP1 chances relative to full-game share.
nhl.first_goal_scorer_share.measurement: Estimate team first-goal probability from per-team scoring hazard h_team(t) in the first 20 minutes (opposing goalie adjusted); then P(player scores first | his team scores first) = early-minutes goal share of the player (goals in first 20 minutes of games where his team scored first, divided by team first goals, shrunk to ixG-based share with k=40). Combine P(player first goal) = P(team first) x share x P(regulation or OT goal occurs). Exclude shootout goals.
free_sources: NHL API play-by-play (first goals with scorer and time)
raw_data: game first-goal event: scorer, time, team, strength
nhl.first_goal_scorer_share.why: Supplies the competing-risk structure for the first-goal contract, which is not a simple ladder rung.

nhl.skater_en_usage.label: Skater extra-attacker and empty-net usage share
nhl.skater_en_usage.mechanism: Share of 6v5 minutes and of empty-net goals scored/assisted by the player, and share of 5v6 defending time.
nhl.skater_en_usage.rationale: Late empty-net goals are credited to a handful of players, and the extra attacker is usually a top forward or defenceman; these minutes are tiny but produce many scoring chances at high conversion, shifting P(1+) and P(2+) for those players in close games.
nhl.skater_en_usage.measurement: From play-by-play identify intervals with goalie pulled (situationCode or inferred) and compute per skater: minutes of 6v5 as extra attacker, goals and assists in those intervals, and share of team EN goals; shrink to team-wide EN goal rate with k=15 EN goals; weight by projected probability of close late game (from game script).
raw_data: goalie-pulled intervals with on-ice skaters and goal credits
nhl.skater_en_usage.why: Explains late-game point production beyond the 5v5 and PP model and helps the multi-point rungs.

nhl.next_man_up_redistribution.label: Next-man-up redistribution after lineup absences
nhl.next_man_up_redistribution.mechanism: Empirical change in TOI, line slot and PP unit for each teammate when a given player is out.
nhl.next_man_up_redistribution.rationale: When a top forward or PP1 member is absent, who inherits his minutes and PP time is team- and coach-specific; the status flag alone does not tell the size of promotion for the candidate whose prop is listed.
nhl.next_man_up_redistribution.measurement: For each team-season find games where player X was absent and compute teammates' change in TOI by state, line number and PP unit versus matched games with X present (matched on rest and home/away); shrink team-specific redistribution toward league position-slot priors with k=8 absence games; as-of rule uses only games before the market time. Output delta-TOI and delta-PP-share per teammate for the current absence scenario.
raw_data: player-game TOI by state, lines, PP units, absence flags
nhl.next_man_up_redistribution.why: Converts injury news into the specific promoted player's minutes, the key personnel effect in prop ladders.

nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.label: Power-play termination and unit-time split
nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.mechanism: Expected PP goals per penalty given that a minor ends on a goal and PP1/PP2 share the clock.
nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.rationale: PP time is not additive: a two-minute minor ends when the power-play team scores, so goals per PP are concave in minutes, and the first unit plays roughly the first 60-80 seconds, so PP1 production dominates short power plays. Using PP time x rate overstates multi-goal PP games and misallocates credit among players.
nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.measurement: From play-by-play, for each team and season compute: (a) conversion per PP opportunity (minor penalties only, excluding coincident and 4v4 states), (b) hazard of a PP goal as a function of elapsed PP seconds in 15-second bins, (c) PP1 share of PP time as a function of elapsed seconds, (d) PP goal share by unit. Shrink team hazard to league with k=150 PP opportunities and 2-season half-life. Expected PP goals = sum over expected penalties of integral hazard x survival; keep major and double-minor cases separate.
free_sources: NHL API play-by-play with penalty events and situationCode
raw_data: penalty events (type, minutes), PP start/end, goals with strength state, shift data for unit membership
nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.why: Skater production on the power play is limited by the first-unit share and termination of minors on a goal; PP1 membership is worth more than raw PP minutes.

nhl.ratings_script_distribution.label: Ratings-only pregame score-path distribution (lead/trail/tied time shares and entering-state matrix)
nhl.ratings_script_distribution.mechanism: Simulated from team goal rates alone, the distribution of score states by period and the share of 60 minutes spent leading, trailing or tied shapes shot volume, star deployment, pull timing and empty-net goals without ever touching a price.
nhl.ratings_script_distribution.rationale: The catalog nhl.game_script_prob derives its win probability from ratings AND the market line, so it is contaminated by the benchmark. This replacement is built only from market-free inputs: it keeps the useful scenario-probability content (conditional state mixtures, not a single win probability) while leaving the market line as a comparison target. The subtle point is that the object needed is a distribution over states, not one number.
nhl.ratings_script_distribution.measurement: For each team, set expected 5v5 and special-teams goal rates for the game as lambda_i = league mean x (attack_i x defence_j adjusted xG ratings, shrunk with prior_to_current_blend where available, or ratings built from score-adjusted xGF/xGA per 60 over a 40-game EWMA with 20-game half-life shrunk 25 games toward league mean) x goalie factor (confirmed or probability-weighted starter GSAx per 60 shrunk 1000 shots) plus a home-ice constant estimated from the last 5 seasons. Simulate 20000 games with a negative-binomial goal process with the fitted dispersion, event times drawn from a time-varying rate with score effects, a pull rule at the coach-specific trailing time, and OT 3v3 play. Output per game: P(lead/tied/trail) entering each period, expected minutes in each score state, P(margin>=2 entering the third), and expected 6v5 minutes per team. As-of timestamp: latest ratings and confirmed or probabilistic starter before puck drop; never include any sportsbook or Kalshi price.
free_sources: Natural Stat Trick team game logs
NHL API play-by-play for pull times (api-web.nhle.com)
raw_data: team-game 5v5 and special-teams xGF/xGA per 60 with score and venue splits
goalie GSAx by game and shots faced
coach-specific goalie-pull times from play-by-play
period-by-period score history per game
nhl.ratings_script_distribution.why: Gives the contract a market-free script latent (state mixture and entering-state matrix) so that benchmark prices remain an independent yardstick.

nhl.skater_ot_3v3_exposure.label: Skater overtime 3v3 exposure and point rate
nhl.skater_ot_3v3_exposure.mechanism: Overtime adds a short 3v3 stretch only in games tied after 60 minutes, where stars play very heavy minutes and points come at a much higher rate per minute than at 5v5.
nhl.skater_ot_3v3_exposure.rationale: KXNHLFIRSTGOAL explicitly counts overtime goals and the N+ ladder text does not exclude them, so for stars the OT block adds a few percent to the first rung. The effect is small per game but systematic for top forwards, and zero in games decided in regulation.
nhl.skater_ot_3v3_exposure.measurement: P(OT) from the regulation tie model for the pair; per skater, 3v3 minutes per OT game (mean and sd, 3 seasons, shrunk 20 OT games to position-role mean) times point rate per 3v3 minute shrunk to the league rate (k=100 minutes); expected extra points = P(OT) x minutes x rate; add as a mixture component only for contracts whose rules count overtime. As-of: lineup as known pregame.
raw_data: overtime shifts and events by player-game
regulation tie probabilities per game
nhl.skater_ot_3v3_exposure.why: Captures the overtime 3v3 exposure that the single-game ladders and first-goal contract can include but the record omitted.

nhl.toi.reason: Minutes by strength state multiply every rate; projection from lineup and expected script is essential and PP minutes need a compound-count model.

nhl.pp_role.reason: PP unit and slot differentiate similarly rated players; needs the first-unit time share and termination effects to be useful.

nhl.ixg_player.reason: Most stable individual goal baseline; covers the shooter's own chances only, so it is incomplete for assists and points.

nhl.assist_rate.reason: Draft marks it primary but secondary assists have little persistence; primary-assist rate is useful only through IPP and on-ice chance creation.

nhl.linemate_quality.reason: Single-label proxy for the chance-creation effect that on-ice xGF per 60 measures directly and with controls for opponent and zone starts.

nhl.onice_shpct.reason: Used to strip on-ice shooting luck from point and assist rates; helpful regression correction but not a driver itself.

nhl.finishing.reason: Persistent shooter skill exists but is small relative to noise; heavy shrinkage means it changes P(goal) by only a few percent.

nhl.goalie_start.reason: Mislabelled primary: the opposing goalie moves a skater goal probability by a modest relative amount (magnitude to be measured, not asserted), comparable to finishing differences.

nhl.opp_supp.reason: Position-specific opponent allowance is plausible but noisy per player; team-level suppression plus line matchup captures most of it.

nhl.pk_structure_opp.reason: Matters for PP1 players through opponent PK shape; effect is modest and hard to estimate.

nhl.penalty_rates.reason: Sets PP minutes, which are most valuable and most volatile; matters most for PP1 skaters.

nhl.officials.reason: The penalty_rates definition already includes referee crew tendencies, so this repeats the same effect and should be one term.

nhl.injuries_pit.reason: Availability and promotions change slot; useful only with the redistribution map that gives the size of the promotion.

nhl.game_script_prob.reason: Expected team goals do scale every skater count, but the catalog measurement derives the input from ratings AND the market line, so it is market-contaminated; replaced in stage s5, coverage, interaction 2 and data feeds by the market-free nhl.ratings_script_distribution (state mixture and expected team goals from ratings only).

nhl.stat_dist.reason: Zero-inflated and negative-binomial shape decides P(2+) and P(3+); the draft marks it secondary but the mapping from mean to rungs depends on it.

nhl.scratch_void_risk.reason: The rules text only says an "active" skater who never enters settles at the last fair market price; it does not say how a scratched or ruled-out skater resolves. If scratches resolve No or void, lineup-confirmation timing is first-order for YES probability, so the input is kept as secondary pending the contract question pp5.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Consistency of Kalshi rung prices is a diagnostic of quotes, not a cause of player scoring.

m.rules_text.reason: Mislabelled context: shootout exclusion, fair-price rule and the half-open ten-minute window change the target event.

nhl.early_window_goal_rate.reason: Defined for KXNHLF10G, which the final series assignment moved to game_events (now carried there); no single-game skater ladder here depends on the either-team ten-minute window.

nhl.games_played_hazard.reason: A season-level opportunity cap for KXNHLSEASONPPTS, which moved to the season-counting archetype; single-game ladders use same-day availability (injuries_pit, scratch_void_risk) instead.

nhl.player_season_points_projection.reason: Season points projection served only KXNHLSEASONPPTS, now owned by unreg:team_and_player_season_counting (stage s6 there); no single-game contract in this archetype uses a season total.

interactions.mechanism: PP production is the product of the unit's share of power-play time, penalties drawn and PK concession, and unit share is front-loaded while a goal ends the penalty, so extra penalty minutes yield fewer extra PP1 chances than the product of averages suggests.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate PP points per PP opportunity against PP seconds elapsed and compare with a time x rate model for PP1 and PP2 skaters.

interactions.mechanism: Expected points are on-ice goals for times the skater's credit share; a player with average individual shooting but elite linemates and high IPP outproduces what ixG says, and the two factors multiply rather than add.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress points per game on log on-ice xGF and log IPP and compare to an additive model on holdout seasons.

interactions.mechanism: The 2+ and 3+ rungs scale convexly with team goals: a three-point game requires team goals of at least two and the star on ice for most of them, so a rise in team total lifts P(3+) several times faster than P(1+).
interactions.how_to_test: Compute P(points>=k) by team goal bins and fit the elasticity of each rung to team goals.

interactions.mechanism: An absence only helps the next man if he inherits power-play slots, not just even-strength minutes; the promotion of a depth forward to PP1 changes his point rate by a multiple while an even-strength promotion changes it little.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare production of promoted players across promotions that include versus exclude PP1 time.

interactions.mechanism: First goalscorer requires a first goal at all and an early power play makes the scorer drawn from PP1; the early penalty process and the scorer share interact, so top-line shares at 5v5 understate the first-goal chances of PP1 players.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute player first-goal share separately for first goals scored on the power play versus even strength.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating: P(goal>=1) = 1 - exp(-lambda)
nonlinearities.why: At lambda about 0.3 the probability is about 26 percent, and each added 0.1 of expected goals adds less than the one before; linear features on ixG overstate the high-end players and understate the 2+ rung.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise: power-play minutes weigh more than even-strength minutes
nonlinearities.why: A minute on the power play carries roughly two to three times the scoring rate of an even-strength minute, and blowout compression cuts even-strength minutes but not PP minutes, so total TOI is a poor linear predictor.

nonlinearities.shape: Zero-inflated count with thin right tail
nonlinearities.why: Assist counts have a mass at zero larger than Poisson and heavier tails when the team scores many goals; threshold rungs at 2+ and 3+ are sensitive to this shape more than to the mean.

contract.settlement_definition: No live Kalshi series exists for NHL skater shots on goal, so there is no rules text. The blueprint assumes an 'N+ shots on goal' ladder analogous to the live KXNHLGOAL, KXNHLAST and KXNHLPTS ladders, settling on the official recorded shots on goal for the named skater in the listed game; by analogy a skater who is active but never enters would settle at the last fair price, and whether overtime shots and shootout attempts count would need to be read from the actual rules when a series lists. All of this is an inference from sibling contracts, not observed text.
variants_and_edge_cases: Official SOG definition: shots that are saved or score are recorded by the league scorer; blocked shots and misses are not shots on goal, so the settlement depends on the scorer's judgement and on the recording practice of the arena.

Overtime and shootout: 3v3 overtime shots are ordinary game shots and plausibly count, whereas shootout attempts are not counted in official SOG; neither is confirmed by any rules text for this archetype.

Ladder construction by analogy: nested thresholds (1+, 2+, 3+, 4+, ...) with a monotone probability curve, so the rungs for one player must be mutually consistent and ladder consistency can be used only as a diagnostic.

Player status: active-but-never-enters, healthy scratch and mid-game injury (a player leaves after one shift) lead to different realised counts; the sibling rule would settle the first case at fair price and the last on counted shots.
contract.settlement_data_source: Assumed: official NHL box score player shots on goal (the NHL stats API exposes player shot counts in the boxscore; SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for field naming and revision behaviour).

mechanism.summary: A skater's recorded shots on goal are the output of four multiplicative stages. Exposure: whether he plays and for how many minutes in each strength state, with power-play time the highest-rate minutes. Volume: his attempt rate per minute, which depends on role (forward in the slot, defenceman at the point, PP1 shooter), on linemates who compete for the same shots, and on the team's overall volume against this opponent. Conversion: the fraction of attempts that reach the net rather than being blocked or missing the target, which differs sharply by position and by the opponent's blocking tendency. Counting: the official scorer's decisions. The count is overdispersed because script, penalties and linemate changes move volume and accuracy together, and ladders at 3+ or 4+ sit in the tail for most skaters, so the mean and the dispersion jointly determine rung probabilities.

stages.name: Availability and role slot
stages.description: Shots depend on whether the skater plays, which line he is on, and whether he holds a first power-play unit slot; a promoted depth forward or a returning star changes his role within a game, and an injury during the game truncates exposure. Lineup is fixed mostly at warmups, and replacement of a teammate redistributes shot opportunities inside the line and the unit, so the player's expected volume must be updated when linemates change.
stages.distribution: Discrete lineup scenarios per team; within each, an exposure mean and a probability of mid-game truncation of order 1-2 percent.

stages.name: Minutes by strength state
stages.description: Expected SOG equals even-strength minutes times the even-strength SOG rate plus power-play minutes times the much higher PP rate. Power-play minutes depend on penalties the opponent takes and on the unit's share of each power play, and blowouts compress stars' even-strength minutes. Projected TOI by state is therefore the basic scale of the count and has a heavy right tail from extra power plays.
stages.distribution: Minutes roughly normal at even strength (sd 2-3 min) and compound-Poisson on the power play; PP minutes are highest-variance.

stages.name: Attempt volume and shot-share within the unit
stages.description: Attempt rate per minute reflects role: forwards who play in the slot and take rebounds, defencemen shooting from the point, and PP shooters; it varies with linemates because shot shares sum within a unit, and with the opponent's suppression of volume. Expressing volume as a share of team shots while on ice and multiplying by team volume stabilises estimates, as shares persist more than raw per-60 rates.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed count (negative binomial) with a skater-specific mean of 1.5-4 and variance about 1.3-1.8 times the mean.

stages.name: Attempt-to-SOG conversion and official counting
stages.description: Only unblocked, on-target attempts are shots on goal: defencemen's point shots are blocked more often, forwards in the slot are blocked less but miss more often, and opposing teams differ in blocking. After conversion, the official scorer applies the definition, and arenas can differ in how generously they record. The threshold contract then reads the count at k.
stages.distribution: Binomial thinning of attempts with success probability about 0.5-0.65 (position dependent); recording noise adds a small additional variance.

settlement_contract.note: No rules text exists for this archetype (NO_LIVE_SERIES): settlement mechanics are only the assumed official-SOG recording and OT counting, covered conditionally by these two inputs; the actual contract wording is the open item sg1.

officiating_rules.note: Referee crew affects the number of power plays, which is already inside the penalty input and the power-play minutes stage; apart from that, the scorer's counting decision is the only officiating effect and is handled as an arena recording factor.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach influence on a single skater's shots arrives through line combinations, power-play unit and minutes, all of which are modelled directly; no additional coach-level term is separately identifiable for a single-game count.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Fatigue and standings stakes act through lineup decisions and minutes, which the TOI and availability inputs already carry; the per-minute shot rate of a player who plays is not materially changed by schedule.

nhl.sog_share_on_ice.label: Skater share of team shots on goal while on ice, by strength state
nhl.sog_share_on_ice.mechanism: Player's SOG divided by team SOG during his minutes at even strength and on the power play.
nhl.sog_share_on_ice.rationale: Team shot volume against a specific opponent can be projected from team models; the player's share of that volume while on ice is more persistent than his raw per-60 rate because it removes team-level shocks. It also captures role as a shooter versus a playmaker.
nhl.sog_share_on_ice.measurement: For each skater and state compute share = player SOG / team SOG while the player is on ice, over a 3-season window weighted 0.5/0.3/0.2, shrunk to position-and-line priors with k=40 team shots; project expected SOG = (team SOG per 60 in state projected for the pairing) x (state minutes/60) x share, then sum across states. Update shares when linemate composition changes using the reallocation input.
free_sources: NHL API play-by-play (shot events with shooter and on-ice players)
Natural Stat Trick individual and on-ice tables
raw_data: shot events with shooter id, on-ice teammates, strength state
nhl.sog_share_on_ice.why: Separates team-level volume from the skater's role share so lineup changes and opponent volume are handled correctly.

nhl.shot_share_reallocation.label: Shot-share reallocation within a line or power-play unit
nhl.shot_share_reallocation.mechanism: Change in a skater's share of unit shots when a linemate or PP unit mate is absent or replaced.
nhl.shot_share_reallocation.rationale: Shot shares in a unit sum to one: when the high-volume shooter is out, remaining players' shares rise by the vacated amount in proportion to their usage, not equally; the promoted player also changes his own rate by the quality of the replacement. Status flags do not tell the size.
nhl.shot_share_reallocation.measurement: From team-season games with a unit member out compute each teammate's share before and after, using matched control games (same opponent tier, rest); estimate the pass-through coefficient beta = d(share_j)/d(vacated share) per position, shrink team estimates to league with k=10 games; apply to the current absence scenario. As-of rule uses lineups published at the time of prediction. Caveat: per-team samples of games with a given unit member absent are small (typically 5-20 games per season), so pool teams by role cluster, estimate beta at league-by-position level and use team deviations only when more than 15 absence games exist.
raw_data: unit membership by game, shot events by shooter, absence flags
nhl.shot_share_reallocation.why: Gives the exact change in the listed skater's SOG expectation from teammate absences, which matter more in this market than the injury flag itself.

nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.label: Power-play termination and unit-time split
nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.mechanism: Expected PP goals per penalty given that a minor ends on a goal and PP1/PP2 share the clock.
nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.rationale: PP time is not additive: a two-minute minor ends when the power-play team scores, so goals per PP are concave in minutes, and the first unit plays roughly the first 60-80 seconds, so PP1 production dominates short power plays. Using PP time x rate overstates multi-goal PP games and misallocates credit among players.
nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.measurement: From play-by-play, for each team and season compute: (a) conversion per PP opportunity (minor penalties only, excluding coincident and 4v4 states), (b) hazard of a PP goal as a function of elapsed PP seconds in 15-second bins, (c) PP1 share of PP time as a function of elapsed seconds, (d) PP goal share by unit. Shrink team hazard to league with k=150 PP opportunities and 2-season half-life. Expected PP goals = sum over expected penalties of integral hazard x survival; keep major and double-minor cases separate.
free_sources: NHL API play-by-play with penalty events and situationCode
raw_data: penalty events (type, minutes), PP start/end, goals with strength state, shift data for unit membership
nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.why: Shots on the power play are concentrated in the first unit's initial seconds and the penalty ends on a goal, so PP shots per penalty is concave in minutes and PP1 shooters dominate.

nhl.arena_sog_recording_factor.label: Arena-level SOG recording factor
nhl.arena_sog_recording_factor.mechanism: Home-arena effect on recorded shots on goal after controlling for teams.
nhl.arena_sog_recording_factor.rationale: Official scorers record SOG; arenas can differ systematically, but the size for SOG is smaller and less certain than for hits or giveaways. A measured factor lets the model decide whether venue matters rather than assuming it.
nhl.arena_sog_recording_factor.measurement: Fit a mixed model log(SOG_game) = team offence + team defence + arena effect + season, using all games from 2015-16 on, with the arena random effect shrunk with prior sd 0.03; always use the shrunk posterior mean for every arena (never a significance cutoff, which would bias the retained estimates upward). Report the posterior sd alongside and re-estimate each season, because tracking and scorer changes alter bias.
raw_data: game-level SOG for each team with arena id
nhl.arena_sog_recording_factor.why: Official SOG is a scorer-recorded count, so any arena-level recording factor shifts counts directly for thresholds, and the claim must be tested before being used.

nhl.ot_shot_exposure.label: Overtime shot exposure given regulation tie probability
nhl.ot_shot_exposure.mechanism: Expected extra shots faced in overtime weighted by probability of a tie.
nhl.ot_shot_exposure.rationale: Overtime is a 3v3 period with high shot density that can add several shots to a goalie's count; its expected contribution is P(OT) times shots per OT period, which can push a goalie across a threshold. It enters only if the contract counts OT, which is not stated.
nhl.ot_shot_exposure.measurement: Estimate team-pair P(regulation tie) from the tie model and shots on goal per 3v3 five-minute period from NHL play-by-play 2015-16 on (pooled mean and sd, team adjustments shrunk with k=200 overtime minutes); expected extra saves = P(tie) x shots_per_OT x (1 - OT goal prob); when playoff 5v5 OT applies use hazard-based shots per 20 minutes.
raw_data: OT shot events with strength, team, goalie
nhl.ot_shot_exposure.why: If overtime counts, 3v3 produces several shots for top skaters in a short period and shifts the 4+ rungs for stars in games with high tie probability.

nhl.ratings_script_distribution.label: Ratings-only pregame score-path distribution (lead/trail/tied time shares and entering-state matrix)
nhl.ratings_script_distribution.mechanism: Simulated from team goal rates alone, the distribution of score states by period and the share of 60 minutes spent leading, trailing or tied shapes shot volume, star deployment, pull timing and empty-net goals without ever touching a price.
nhl.ratings_script_distribution.rationale: The catalog nhl.game_script_prob derives its win probability from ratings AND the market line, so it is contaminated by the benchmark. This replacement is built only from market-free inputs: it keeps the useful scenario-probability content (conditional state mixtures, not a single win probability) while leaving the market line as a comparison target. The subtle point is that the object needed is a distribution over states, not one number.
nhl.ratings_script_distribution.measurement: For each team, set expected 5v5 and special-teams goal rates for the game as lambda_i = league mean x (attack_i x defence_j adjusted xG ratings, shrunk with prior_to_current_blend where available, or ratings built from score-adjusted xGF/xGA per 60 over a 40-game EWMA with 20-game half-life shrunk 25 games toward league mean) x goalie factor (confirmed or probability-weighted starter GSAx per 60 shrunk 1000 shots) plus a home-ice constant estimated from the last 5 seasons. Simulate 20000 games with a negative-binomial goal process with the fitted dispersion, event times drawn from a time-varying rate with score effects, a pull rule at the coach-specific trailing time, and OT 3v3 play. Output per game: P(lead/tied/trail) entering each period, expected minutes in each score state, P(margin>=2 entering the third), and expected 6v5 minutes per team. As-of timestamp: latest ratings and confirmed or probabilistic starter before puck drop; never include any sportsbook or Kalshi price.
free_sources: Natural Stat Trick team game logs
NHL API play-by-play for pull times (api-web.nhle.com)
raw_data: team-game 5v5 and special-teams xGF/xGA per 60 with score and venue splits
goalie GSAx by game and shots faced
coach-specific goalie-pull times from play-by-play
period-by-period score history per game
nhl.ratings_script_distribution.why: Gives the contract a market-free script latent (state mixture and entering-state matrix) so that benchmark prices remain an independent yardstick.

nhl.shot_rate.reason: Core per-minute rate; should be decomposed into team volume and player share, and strength-split with heavy shrinkage to avoid small-sample noise.

nhl.toi.reason: Scale factor of the count; PP and blowout effects require a state-specific projection rather than total TOI.

nhl.pp_role.reason: PP shooter slot has a rate several times the even-strength rate; the role is more informative than team PP efficiency.

nhl.shot_block_miss.reason: SOG is only the on-target subset of attempts; block and miss rates differ by position and opponent, so it is essential for conversion.

nhl.dman_shot_profile.reason: Defencemen shots are role and PP dependent; useful for the subset of skaters who are defencemen but not a general driver.

nhl.opp_supp.reason: Position-level opponent suppression is noisy at the individual level; team-level shots allowed explains most of the effect.

nhl.shots_against.reason: Mislabelled secondary: the opponent's shots allowed set team volume that the player's share multiplies, so it is a first-order driver of the count.

nhl.venue.reason: The catalog venue label bundles SOG counting bias with home advantage; the counting bias is the same quantity as the new arena factor, and since no rules text exists (NO_LIVE_SERIES, sg1) the claim that it matters is untested. Home-ice is not separately claimed for a single skater count.

nhl.score_state.reason: Trailing teams shoot more and leaders less, but effects are modest and mostly visible in the third period. The catalog measurement integrates score-state rates over 'pregame win probability and total'; that must be the ratings-only nhl.ratings_script_distribution, not a market-implied win probability or total.

nhl.game_script_prob.reason: Catalog measurement derives win probability from ratings and the market line, so it is market-contaminated and its effect on one skater count is small; replaced in stage s2, coverage, interaction 4 and data feeds by the market-free nhl.ratings_script_distribution.

nhl.penalty_rates.reason: Determines power-play minutes for PP shooters; matters more for the tail than the mean.

nhl.lines.reason: Linemates determine the share of shots in the unit and the quality of shots; needs the reallocation map to be actionable.

nhl.zone_start_share.reason: Zone starts are partly a consequence of usage already captured in per-60 rates and role; its separate effect is confounded and small.

nhl.toi_trend.reason: Recent role changes precede season averages; useful when a player has been promoted but less so for stable players.

nhl.injuries_pit.reason: Lineup news changes TOI and shot share; the draft's treatment of late scratches rests on a rule that has not been observed.

nhl.stat_dist.reason: Mislabelled secondary: the count distribution (negative binomial with role-specific dispersion) maps the mean to 2+ to 5+ rungs and is first order.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Nested-rung consistency of prices is a quote diagnostic and says nothing about shots; no ladder exists yet for this archetype.

nhl.shot_location.reason: Danger-zone mix affects goal probability, not the number of shots on goal; for a SOG count threshold it is largely irrelevant.

interactions.mechanism: Expected SOG rises with the number of power plays, and PP1 shooters convert minutes to shots at several times the even-strength rate, so uncertainty in penalty counts fattens the right tail for PP1 shooters but not for penalty-kill defencemen.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute realised SOG for PP1 shooters by number of power plays in the game and compare with depth forwards.

interactions.mechanism: Blocks reduce defencemen's point shots far more than forwards' slot shots, so an opponent with strong blocking suppresses defencemen's SOG more; the opponent block rate should be applied conditional on position and shot origin.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate opponent block rate coefficients separately for forwards and defencemen in an attempts-to-SOG model.

interactions.mechanism: Expected SOG equals team volume times the player's share of volume; a high-share forward against a defence that allows few shots has a mean far below his season average, and share and team volume are not additive.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare predictions from team-volume x share against a per-60 rate model on out-of-sample games.

interactions.mechanism: When the unit's high-volume shooter is absent, remaining skaters' shares rise by the vacated amount in proportion to their usage; the effect is conditional on who is out and on whether the replacement is a shooter or a passer.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate share change for linemates by absent-player type in games with and without that player.

interactions.mechanism: Stars on the leading team lose minutes only when the lead reaches about three goals; below that threshold their shot count is unaffected, while trailing teams' stars add shots late, so the response of SOG to lead is a threshold, not linear.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin by final goal difference and compare TOI and SOG of top-line skaters on winning versus losing teams.

interactions.mechanism: If an arena records shots more generously, the effect scales with the number of attempts that reach the net and applies to home and visiting skaters alike, so it multiplies the player rate rather than adding a constant; the effect should be larger for high-volume shooters.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the arena random effect on visiting-team skater SOG per 60 and test whether the effect scales with the player baseline rate (log-link slope near one) rather than being additive.

nonlinearities.shape: Negative binomial: tail grows with the mean convexly
nonlinearities.why: For a mean of 2.8 the probability of 4+ is about a quarter and of 5+ a tenth, and these rungs are far more sensitive to dispersion than 1+ or 2+, so a Poisson assumption misprices high rungs.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise linear with PP minutes carrying a higher slope
nonlinearities.why: A power-play minute yields two to three times the SOG of an even-strength minute, so total TOI is a poor linear predictor and the minutes must be split by state.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating conversion bounded between 0 and 1
nonlinearities.why: Attempt-to-SOG conversion cannot exceed one and varies in a narrow band, so improvements in volume translate to SOG linearly but differences in block rate apply multiplicatively.
