contract.settlement_definition: No live Kalshi series exists for NHL player head-to-head, so there is no rules text. The blueprint describes a contract that pays YES if player A records more of a named stat (points, shots on goal or saves) than player B in the listed game, with tie handling and the treatment of a non-playing player to be set by the rules. By analogy to the live prop ladders a skater who is active but never enters would settle at the last fair price; whether a tie is a push, a No, or a fair-price void is unknown, and that single rule changes the effective probability materially.
variants_and_edge_cases: Tie treatment: for low-count stats (points, saves of goalies with few shots against) a tie is likely, a large share of pairs for points (the magnitude is an unsourced guess, to be measured); if ties settle No, the contract is about P(A>B) not P(A>B | no tie), and each reading changes fair price by several points.

Pair composition: teammates (shared script, goalie, goals) versus opponents (opposing script, shared pace) have correlation of opposite sign, so the same marginal means give different outcome probabilities by pair type.

Stat type: points (credit-based, discrete, zero-heavy), shots on goal (volume count, overdispersed) and saves (goalie exposure) have different distributions; goalies as opponents also face the exposure and pull rules.
Participation: either player not playing or leaving early (injury after one shift) needs a stated rule; the blueprint says DNP rules per contract, none observed.
contract.settlement_data_source: Assumed: official NHL box score player statistics (points, shots on goal, saves); rule for ties and non-participation unobserved.

mechanism.summary: A head-to-head contract compares two counts, so the outcome is the sign of D = X_A - X_B, and the relevant object is the joint distribution of the pair, not the two marginals. Each marginal comes from a single-player model: minutes by state, per-minute rate and credit structure for points, shot volume and conversion for shots, exposure and shot flow for saves. The pair is then coupled through shared factors: teammates share script, goalie, linemates and goals; opponents share pace and have opposed scripts; two linemates also co-earn points on the same goal. The discrete difference has large tie mass for low counts, so the tie rule and the DNP rule (both unobserved, no series exists) would change the contract's probability by several points. Lineup news on either player can void the comparison or flip the sign of the expected difference.

stages.name: Participation and lineup state for both players
stages.description: The contract is defined only if both players take part, and the rule for a non-playing player (void, fair price or loss) determines how much availability risk is priced. Lineup news on either player changes roles: a linemate's absence promotes one and not the other, and an injury during the game truncates one count. The joint availability states (both play, A only, B only, neither) have separate distributions of D.
stages.distribution: Four joint participation states with probabilities mostly concentrated on both-play; the remaining mass is a fair-price or void component set by the rule.

stages.name: Marginal expectation and dispersion of each player's stat
stages.description: Each player's mean comes from a single-player model: for skater points on-ice goal exposure and the credit share, for skater shots team volume and shot share, for goalies shot flow and exposure minutes. Role differences such as PP1 membership produce much of the gap in expected counts between two similarly rated players. Dispersion differs across stats and roles and determines the tie mass and the spread of D.
stages.distribution: Marginals: points zero-inflated NB with mean 0.4-1.2; shots NB with mean 1.5-4 and dispersion 1.3-1.8; goalie saves NB with mean 24-30.

stages.name: Dependence between the two counts
stages.description: For two teammates the counts share the game's script, the goalie they face and, for points, the very same goals (a linemate scores and the other is assisted), so correlation is positive and the variance of D is lower than the sum of variances. For opponents the shared pace gives mild positive correlation in shots while the opposed script creates negative correlation (the leader's player loses minutes and shots), and goalies on opposing sides have saves that move with the same game total but with opposed script. The sign and size of correlation depends on pair type.
stages.distribution: Bivariate discrete dependence with pair-type-specific correlation: teammates rho about +0.2 to +0.4 for points, opponents rho about -0.05 to +0.1; shared goals produce joint jumps.

stages.name: Difference distribution, tie mass and contract probability
stages.description: The probability of a win for A is P(D>0) possibly renormalised by the tie rule; with small means the discrete mass at D=0 is large, so the distinction between P(A>B) and P(A>B | no tie) is of the order of the price itself. The model must therefore produce an exact pmf of D from the joint count model rather than a normal approximation to the difference of means.
stages.distribution: Discrete pmf of D with a spike at zero; tie probability about 30-40 percent for points, 12-20 percent for shots, about 7-9 percent for goalie saves.

environment.note: Both players compete in the same rink on the same night, so rink, weather and altitude effects cancel in a difference, and the residual arena effect is common to both players' counts.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching changes act on the two players through their lines and PP units, which are modelled directly as role inputs; coach identity is the same for teammates and enters opposing pairs only through team context.

officiating_rules.note: Referee crew affects power plays for both teams; the pair's relative PP exposure is already captured by PP role and unit overlap, so a separate officiating feature adds nothing for the difference.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and standings stakes affect whether a player plays, handled by the availability inputs; conditional on playing, schedule has no pair-specific effect on the difference.

nhl.pair_difference_distribution.label: [Model output, not raw data] Pair difference distribution with tie mass by pair type and stat
nhl.pair_difference_distribution.mechanism: Joint count model for (X_A, X_B) yielding the exact pmf of the difference including P(D=0).
nhl.pair_difference_distribution.rationale: The sign of a difference of two small counts cannot be approximated by comparing means: tie mass, dispersion and pair-specific correlation set the probability. A pair-type-aware joint pmf is the contract's own object and also yields P(A>B | no tie) for rule variants.
nhl.pair_difference_distribution.measurement: Fit bivariate count models per stat (points: zero-inflated NB with a shared-goal term; shots: bivariate NB with correlation; saves: bivariate NB for opposing goalies) with pair-type-specific correlation parameters (same line, same team different line, opponents), estimated from 5 seasons of player-game logs; shrink pair-type correlations to league values with k=300 pair-games; compute pmf of D by convolution, report P(D>0), P(D=0), P(D<0) under both tie rules, and recalibrate on holdout seasons by tie frequency.
raw_data: player-game stat lines for all pairs observed in the same game, with team and line info
nhl.pair_difference_distribution.why: Provides the exact difference distribution and tie mass that the head-to-head contract settles on.

nhl.teammate_point_co_credit.label: Teammate point co-credit rate
nhl.teammate_point_co_credit.mechanism: Probability that a goal on which player A earns a point also gives player B a point, by strength state.
nhl.teammate_point_co_credit.rationale: Two linemates are positively correlated in points because the same goal credits both; this co-credit structure is a source of dependence beyond shared script and reduces the variance of D for teammate pairs.
nhl.teammate_point_co_credit.measurement: From goal events compute for each ordered teammate pair the share of A's points that came on goals where B also earned a point, per strength state, over three seasons with k=30 shared points shrinkage to position-line priors; summarise in a pair-level co-credit coefficient used in the joint count model as the shared-goal Poisson component.
raw_data: goal events with scorer and assist ids by strength state
nhl.teammate_point_co_credit.why: The positive correlation of linemates is the main reason a teammate comparison is tighter than an opponent comparison with equal means.

nhl.ipp_by_state.label: Individual points percentage by strength state (points per on-ice goal for)
nhl.ipp_by_state.mechanism: Share of team goals scored while on ice on which the player is credited with a goal or assist.
nhl.ipp_by_state.rationale: Points are credited on team goals, so expected points equal on-ice goals for times the share of those on which the skater is credited; this share is far more stable than assists per game and is role dependent (forwards on scoring lines high, defencemen lower, PP1 shooters very high).
nhl.ipp_by_state.measurement: For each skater and strength state (EV, PP) compute IPP = (goals + assists) / on-ice goals for, using 3 seasons weighted by 0.5/0.3/0.2 and shrunk to position-and-role priors with k=25 on-ice goals; separate primary and secondary assist components, shrinking secondary toward position mean with k=60; apply per-60 conversion: expected points per game = sum over states of (on-ice GF/60 x state TOI/60 x IPP_state).
free_sources: NHL API play-by-play (goals with scorer and assists, on-ice players)
raw_data: goal events with scorer, assist1, assist2, on-ice skaters by strength state
nhl.ipp_by_state.why: For a points comparison the credit share relative to team on-ice goals separates roles with equal TOI, e.g. a playmaking centre versus a defenceman on the same line.

nhl.sog_share_on_ice.label: Skater share of team shots on goal while on ice, by strength state
nhl.sog_share_on_ice.mechanism: Player's SOG divided by team SOG during his minutes at even strength and on the power play.
nhl.sog_share_on_ice.rationale: Team shot volume against a specific opponent can be projected from team models; the player's share of that volume while on ice is more persistent than his raw per-60 rate because it removes team-level shocks. It also captures role as a shooter versus a playmaker.
nhl.sog_share_on_ice.measurement: For each skater and state compute share = player SOG / team SOG while the player is on ice, over a 3-season window weighted 0.5/0.3/0.2, shrunk to position-and-line priors with k=40 team shots; project expected SOG = (team SOG per 60 in state projected for the pairing) x (state minutes/60) x share, then sum across states. Update shares when linemate composition changes using the reallocation input.
free_sources: NHL API play-by-play (shot events with shooter and on-ice players)
Natural Stat Trick individual and on-ice tables
raw_data: shot events with shooter id, on-ice teammates, strength state
nhl.sog_share_on_ice.why: For a shots comparison the share of team volume is more stable than raw per-60 rate and controls for the opponent shot volume that both players share.

nhl.goalie_minutes_in_net_dist.label: Goalie minutes-in-net distribution (entry, pull and overtime)
nhl.goalie_minutes_in_net_dist.mechanism: Probability distribution of the named goalie's exposure in minutes and the relief goalie's partial exposure.
nhl.goalie_minutes_in_net_dist.rationale: The settlement rule makes exposure part of the contract: no entry -> fair-price, entry -> own saves only. Exposure is neither 60 nor zero; pulls and relief appearances create a mass at partial minutes. This is a distribution, not a scalar start probability.
nhl.goalie_minutes_in_net_dist.measurement: From box scores since 2015-16 build for each goalie the empirical pmf of minutes, conditional on starting: P(pulled before 40:00), P(pulled in 40-55), P(full + OT). Shrink each goalie's pull rate to team-coach and league rates with k=25 starts; make pull hazard depend on goals allowed in the first period (0, 1, 2, 3+). Combine with P(start | rest, schedule, report) from the forecast to get an overall mixture, and mark the no-start component as fair-price (excluded from the YES/NO distribution).
free_sources: NHL API boxscore (TOI and shots per goalie)
raw_data: goalie-game: starter flag, TOI, shots faced, goals against, relief entry time, pull reason if recorded
nhl.goalie_minutes_in_net_dist.why: A goalie comparison needs each goalie's exposure distribution: pulled or non-playing goalies drive tie and void probability.

nhl.opp_sog_for_rate.label: Opponent shots-on-goal-for rate by strength state, score adjusted
nhl.opp_sog_for_rate.mechanism: Opponent's own shot-on-goal generation per 60 at EV and on the power play.
nhl.opp_sog_for_rate.rationale: The draft carries opponent xG (a quality measure) and the defence's suppression, but saves count shots on goal, so the opponent's volume of on-target shots, separate from danger, is the first-order driver. xG weights shots by quality and understates the effect of low-danger volume teams.
nhl.opp_sog_for_rate.measurement: Per team compute SOG for per 60 at 5v5 (score-and-venue adjusted via regression of SOG rate on score differential bins) and at 5v4, with 2-season half-life 40 games and shrink to league with k=15 games; project game SOG faced = EV_rate_opp x defence_adjustment x projected EV minutes + PP_rate_opp x projected PP minutes. Use log-additive combination with opponent defence SOG-against: log E = mu + off_opp + def_team.
free_sources: Natural Stat Trick team SOG splits
raw_data: team-game SOG by strength state and score state
nhl.opp_sog_for_rate.why: Two opposing goalies face different opponents; the saves difference is dominated by the difference in opponent SOG-for volumes.

nhl.ratings_script_distribution.label: Ratings-only pregame score-path distribution (lead/trail/tied time shares and entering-state matrix)
nhl.ratings_script_distribution.mechanism: Simulated from team goal rates alone, the distribution of score states by period and the share of 60 minutes spent leading, trailing or tied shapes shot volume, star deployment, pull timing and empty-net goals without ever touching a price.
nhl.ratings_script_distribution.rationale: The catalog nhl.game_script_prob derives its win probability from ratings AND the market line, so it is contaminated by the benchmark. This replacement is built only from market-free inputs: it keeps the useful scenario-probability content (conditional state mixtures, not a single win probability) while leaving the market line as a comparison target. The subtle point is that the object needed is a distribution over states, not one number.
nhl.ratings_script_distribution.measurement: For each team, set expected 5v5 and special-teams goal rates for the game as lambda_i = league mean x (attack_i x defence_j adjusted xG ratings, shrunk with prior_to_current_blend where available, or ratings built from score-adjusted xGF/xGA per 60 over a 40-game EWMA with 20-game half-life shrunk 25 games toward league mean) x goalie factor (confirmed or probability-weighted starter GSAx per 60 shrunk 1000 shots) plus a home-ice constant estimated from the last 5 seasons. Simulate 20000 games with a negative-binomial goal process with the fitted dispersion, event times drawn from a time-varying rate with score effects, a pull rule at the coach-specific trailing time, and OT 3v3 play. Output per game: P(lead/tied/trail) entering each period, expected minutes in each score state, P(margin>=2 entering the third), and expected 6v5 minutes per team. As-of timestamp: latest ratings and confirmed or probabilistic starter before puck drop; never include any sportsbook or Kalshi price.

nhl.toi.reason: Minutes by state differ between players and determine expected counts; for pairs the difference in PP minutes matters most.

nhl.shot_rate.reason: Core shot rate for the shots variant; should be decomposed into team volume and share, which this contract needs because both players share the game volume.

nhl.ixg_player.reason: Useful for goals and points comparisons but individual xG omits chance creation credited as assists; secondary for points pairs.

nhl.pp_role.reason: Differences in PP unit and slot give one player a large share of the high-yield minutes; overlap in the same unit gives both the same PP opportunities.

nhl.lines.reason: Same-line pairs are positively correlated, different lines are not; the pair type determines the dependence model rather than the mean.

nhl.opp_supp.reason: Teammates face the same opponent so the term cancels; for opposing pairs it is a minor modifier already contained in team-level suppression.

nhl.goalie_start.reason: The opposing starter affects both teammates equally and each opponent pair differently; effect on the difference is small except for goalie-vs-goalie pairs.

nhl.joint_outcome_correlation.reason: Right object, but a single pooled correlation is wrong: sign and size differ for linemates, same-team different lines and opponents, so it needs to be pair-type specific.

nhl.stat_dist.reason: Mislabelled secondary: difference distribution and tie mass require count shapes and a joint model; it is first order.

nhl.injuries_pit.reason: Either player's lineup news changes the sign of the expected difference and the participation state.

nhl.scratch_void_risk.reason: Matters only to the extent the rule voids or fair-prices a non-participant; the effect on outcome probability depends on a rule not yet observed.

m.rules_text.reason: Tie and non-participation handling define the target and shift price by several points; none is observed for this archetype.

nhl.score_state.reason: Script affects teammates in common and opponents oppositely; its role is in the sign of the correlation rather than the mean difference. The catalog measurement integrates score-state rates over 'pregame win probability and total'; that must be the ratings-only nhl.ratings_script_distribution, not a market-implied win probability or total.

interactions.mechanism: The correlation between the two players' counts changes sign with pair type: linemates share goals and script so rho is positive and the difference has low variance, whereas opponents share pace but face opposed script so rho is near zero or negative; a pooled correlation misprices both.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate rho separately for same-line, same-team, and opposing pairs and compare out-of-sample deviance with a pooled value.

interactions.mechanism: Tie mass of the difference is a function of the two marginal means: when both players expect counts near zero (points for depth players, saves with few shots) the tie mass is large and the contract mostly prices P(A>B) against a big atom; as means grow the atom shrinks, so the same mean gap implies a larger win probability for high-volume pairs.
interactions.how_to_test: Bin pairs by the sum of expected counts and compare the empirical tie share and P(A>B | no tie) with the fitted discrete difference; how a tie settles is a separate rule question (hh1) and is not tested here.

interactions.mechanism: If both players are on the same power-play unit they receive the same power-play opportunities, so penalty-count uncertainty shifts both counts together and mostly cancels in the difference, whereas for players on different units it adds variance of opposite effect; unit overlap decides whether penalty uncertainty matters for the contract.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare variance of D for same-unit and different-unit pairs conditional on penalties.

interactions.mechanism: On a linemate pair the same goal credits both, so points are positively dependent in a way that depends on each player's credit share; for a playmaker versus a shooter the co-credit probability is high and the difference is rarely large.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the distribution of D for linemates with the independent-count prediction and estimate the co-credit term.

interactions.mechanism: A lineup change that moves one player down a line or off the PP crosses a threshold in expected TOI that reverses the sign of the expected difference; the priced effect is a step at confirmation time rather than a gradual drift.
interactions.how_to_test: Measure the change in difference in expected counts at lineup confirmations and the resulting change in the outcome probability.

nonlinearities.shape: Spike at zero in a discrete difference
nonlinearities.why: For small counts the pmf of the difference has a sharp peak at zero, so the win probability for A is not a smooth function of the difference in means near equality; a normal approximation misstates the tie mass.

nonlinearities.shape: Pair-type dependent with sign change
nonlinearities.why: Correlation is positive for linemates and near zero or negative for opponents, so the variance of the difference is a non-monotone function of pair type, and a constant correlation parameter is not valid.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise with PP minutes weighted more heavily
nonlinearities.why: A shift of one PP minute between players changes the expected count by much more than an even-strength minute, so differences in total TOI are less informative than differences in PP minutes.

contract.settlement_definition: No live NHL parlay or combo series appears in the ledger, so there is no rules text. The blueprint describes a single contract that pays only if every named leg (team result, spread, total, player stat) occurs in the same game or slate; its fair price is the joint probability of all legs. Whether a voided or fair-priced leg (for example a non-playing skater) removes the leg, collapses the combo to a fair price or settles it No is unknown and is the single most important settlement unknown, since a prop leg in an NHL game has a non-trivial chance of being voided at fair price under sibling rules. All dependence machinery below (credit kernel, copula, scenario tree) is conditional on the unverified assumption that combos bundle legs of the SAME game; if Kalshi combos are cross-game or cross-sport collections of existing markets, the required inputs reduce to leg marginals, leg logical relations and the void payoff map (pc5).
variants_and_edge_cases: Leg void handling: sibling prop rules settle an active-but-never-enters player at the last fair price; if a combo inherits this, the contract payoff after a void is a different function of the remaining legs, not simply the product of the others.

Logically related legs: nested ladder rungs (points 2+ inside points 1+), a team win with the opponent's spread, or a team total leg with the game total leg are not independent and some combinations are impossible, so the pricing must respect implications and exclusions.

Same-game versus cross-game combos: legs from different games are independent except for shared news, whereas same-game legs share latent game drivers; the structure of the contract decides which model is needed.

Leg settlement differences: a shootout adds one goal to totals and team totals but affects margins differently, and third-period legs exclude overtime; each leg inherits its own rule, so a combo is only as clean as its worst-defined leg.
contract.settlement_data_source: Per-leg official NHL game and player statistics; combo-level resolution rules unobserved.

mechanism.summary: The fair price of a combo is the probability of an intersection, which equals the product of marginals times a dependence factor that depends on shared latent drivers. In an NHL game those drivers are few and identifiable: the goal intensity of each team (pace and quality), the goalie states (starter identity and a within-game quality shock including pulls), the number of power plays, the lineup state of key skaters, and the score path that decides empty-net goals and minutes compression. Player legs follow from team goals via an allocation of goals and assists to the skaters on ice, so the right architecture is one game-level simulation that draws latent states, generates team goal events, allocates credit to players, and reads all legs from the same draw. Dependence is not constant: it grows in the tails (blowouts), switches sign for some leg pairs (goalie saves versus totals), and mis-specification compounds because errors in each leg multiply. Settlement of voided legs changes the payoff structure.

stages.name: Leg catalogue and logical structure
stages.description: Each leg is a threshold on a game statistic: win, margin, total, a team's total, a skater's goals, assists, points or shots, a goalie's saves. Some legs imply or exclude each other: points of two or more imply points of one, a team's win excludes the opponent's win, and a team total over implies a minimum for the game total. These deterministic relations determine part of the joint probability exactly and must be imposed before any correlation is estimated.
stages.distribution: Deterministic implications and exclusions among discrete legs; no free parameter, only structural constraints.

stages.name: Shared latent game drivers
stages.description: The legs are tied by a small set of latent variables: total goal intensity (pace times shot quality), goal differential driven by team strength and script, goalie quality shocks (including an early pull), and the number of power plays. A positive shock to total intensity lifts goals, assists and totals together, while a goalie shock moves the opposing team's scoring and the goalie's own saves in different directions. Their joint distribution defines the correlation structure of all legs.
stages.distribution: Low-dimensional latent vector with heavy tails: goal intensity lognormal-like, goalie shock mixture (normal game versus pulled), power plays Poisson.

stages.name: Conditional player legs given team goals
stages.description: Given the simulated team goals and strength states, each goal is allocated to skaters on the ice with probabilities set by their shot shares and credit shares, so a skater's goals, assists and points are conditional on the team's goals and on his minutes. This creates the positive correlation between a team's win leg and its star's points leg and between team total and player points, and it respects the maximum of three points per goal. Minutes compression in blowouts adds a negative link between margin and star shot counts.
stages.distribution: Allocation is multinomial per goal; conditional on g team goals, a skater's points are a thinned binomial-like count with credit probability near 0.6-0.8 for top forwards.

stages.name: Lineup scenarios and settlement mapping
stages.description: Lineup states are discrete and correlated across legs: a starter goalie change or a star scratch moves several legs at once, and a non-playing prop leg may be voided. The scenario tree gives joint probabilities of these states at the contract's decision time. Payoff then depends on the settlement map for voided legs, which changes the combo from an intersection into a conditional-intersection contract.
stages.distribution: Discrete scenario tree with 4-12 leaves; payoff map piecewise over leg statuses (win, lose, void).

opponent_matchup.note: Matchups between specific teams and players are properties of each leg's marginal model; the combo adds nothing matchup-specific beyond the shared latent drivers, which are captured by team means in the simulation.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching effects enter each leg through team rates, lines and minutes, already part of the marginal leg models; a combo contract does not add a separate coaching mechanism beyond what is in its legs.

environment.note: Rink and travel effects act through team means of each leg and are common across legs in the same game, so they affect the marginals but not the dependence structure beyond what team means carry.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and standings stakes affect lineup and strength states that the scenario tree and team means already carry; no combo-specific schedule mechanism exists.

officiating_rules.note: Referee tendencies shift penalty counts which are part of the shared latent drivers; the combo adds no officiating mechanism of its own beyond the leg-level rules.

nhl.goal_credit_allocation_kernel.label: Goal-credit allocation kernel (probability each skater scores or assists on a team goal)
nhl.goal_credit_allocation_kernel.mechanism: Probability that a skater is credited with the goal, primary or secondary assist, conditional on a team goal at a given strength state and lineup.
nhl.goal_credit_allocation_kernel.rationale: A combo mixing team and player legs needs one coherent mechanism linking team goals to individual stats; a kernel based on on-ice shares and credit shares guarantees consistency and the cap of one goal and two assists per team goal.
nhl.goal_credit_allocation_kernel.measurement: For each skater and strength state (EV, PP, EN) compute: P(on ice | team goal) = team goals scored while on ice / team goals in the state, and P(credit type | on ice, goal) from three seasons of goal events (shrunk to position/line priors with k=30 goals); build for the projected lineup a kernel K[skater, role(goal, A1, A2)] with columns summing to 1 for goals, and at most two assists per goal; in simulation draw each goal's state, then allocate credit by K. Recalibrate so that simulated team assists per goal match league and team averages.
free_sources: NHL API play-by-play (goal credits and on-ice skaters)
raw_data: goal events with on-ice skaters, scorer and assists, strength state
nhl.goal_credit_allocation_kernel.why: Forms the bridge between team-goal legs and player-stat legs so that win, total and points legs come from the same simulated goals.

nhl.lineup_scenario_tree.label: Joint lineup scenario tree (goalies and key skaters)
nhl.lineup_scenario_tree.mechanism: Joint probability over starter goalie for each team and the status of the three or four most influential skaters.
nhl.lineup_scenario_tree.rationale: A single leg's availability probability is not enough: several legs move at once on the same news, and the joint probability of states (e.g., backup in net and star out) is not the product of marginal probabilities because of shared causes such as back-to-backs.
nhl.lineup_scenario_tree.measurement: Define for each team K key players (starting goalie plus top-4 skaters by impact) and enumerate states; estimate P(state) from the team's historical patterns: goalie rotation (consecutive-start rules, back-to-back), injury reports and morning skate evidence; assume independence beyond shared schedule factors unless data show otherwise; limit leaves to those with probability above 1 percent and merge the rest; store each state with its decision-time vintage.
raw_data: lineup reports, goalie starts, injury statuses with timestamps
nhl.lineup_scenario_tree.why: Provides the joint discrete shocks across legs; voided legs and shifted marginals happen on these same states.

nhl.copula_tail_dependence.label: Tail dependence between leg pairs (copula parameters by pair type)
nhl.copula_tail_dependence.mechanism: Dependence in the joint upper and lower tails of leg pairs beyond linear correlation.
nhl.copula_tail_dependence.rationale: Hockey legs show stronger dependence in the tails than in the centre: blowout games produce high totals, large margins and many points together. A Gaussian copula with a pooled correlation underprices joint tail events and overprices central ones.
nhl.copula_tail_dependence.measurement: For each pair type (win-total, win-player points, total-player points, goalie saves-total, total-team total) compute from five seasons of game logs the empirical conditional exceedance chi(u) = P(U>u, V>u)/(1-u) at u = 0.7, 0.8, 0.9 using rank transforms with discrete tie handling; fit Gaussian, Student-t and Clayton copulas by maximum likelihood on the pseudo-observations and choose by out-of-sample joint log-likelihood; shrink pair-type parameters with k=400 games.
free_sources: NHL API player-game and team logs
raw_data: game-level outcomes for all legs: result, margin, total, player stats
nhl.copula_tail_dependence.why: Corrects the Gaussian-correlation shortcut that is the main source of error in joint tails.

nhl.parlay_leg_void_payoff_map.label: Parlay leg-void payoff map
nhl.parlay_leg_void_payoff_map.mechanism: Lookup table mapping each combination of leg statuses (win, lose, void-at-fair-price) to the contract payoff under the rules in force.
nhl.parlay_leg_void_payoff_map.rationale: The fair price depends on what happens to the combo when a leg voids: collapse to fair price, drop the leg, or lose. The same probabilities give different prices under different maps, and none is observed in the sampled rules.
nhl.parlay_leg_void_payoff_map.measurement: From the rules text of each combo series build a table payoff(status vector); where text is missing mark the map as unknown and carry multiple candidate maps (drop-leg, fair-price collapse, lose) with prior weights; compute price under each candidate and report the range; version by rules_text vintage so that changes are visible.
raw_data: rules_primary and rules_secondary per combo series with version
nhl.parlay_leg_void_payoff_map.why: Determines what the combo is worth when a leg voids, which can swing price by more than any modelling edge.

nhl.leg_logical_relations.label: Leg logical-relations map (implications, exclusions, shared ladders)
nhl.leg_logical_relations.mechanism: Deterministic implications and exclusions among legs of the same game.
nhl.leg_logical_relations.rationale: Nested rungs and mutually exclusive outcomes fix part of the joint probability exactly: points 2+ implies points 1+, a team win excludes the opponent win, the spread leg implies the win leg. A correlation model that ignores this can assign probability to impossible combinations.
nhl.leg_logical_relations.measurement: Enumerate for each pair of legs the logical relation under the game's settlement rules (including shootout credit, third-period OT exclusion, and nested player ladders) and store as a matrix of {implies, excludes, independent-by-construction, free}; the simulator rejects draws violating relations and the pricing uses P(A and B) = P(A) for implied and 0 for excluded.
raw_data: leg definitions with period, rung, stat and settlement rules
nhl.leg_logical_relations.why: Prevents impossible or double-counted combinations in the combo price.

interactions.mechanism: P(team wins and star records 2+ points) is much larger than the product of marginals because a win by two or more requires goals and the star is credited on a share of them; the uplift is convex in the number of team goals and falls when blowouts compress the star's minutes.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute P(win and points>=2) by team goals bins and compare with the product and with the simulation.

interactions.mechanism: Hypothesis only: a backup goalie start and a missing star skater on the same team may be linked through back-to-back scheduling and would then move the team win, total and player legs together, so the joint probability of lineup states would not be the product of marginals; the size of the link is not evidenced and should be estimated before use.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the odds ratio between backup-goalie starts and star absences on back-to-backs versus rested games from 5 seasons of lineup data; set the joint tree to independent if the ratio is within noise of one.

interactions.mechanism: In the blowout regime (margin three or more) the legs on total, margin and star points are strongly dependent, whereas in the centre the dependence is weak; a single correlation parameter underprices the tail combinations that parlays most often bundle.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit conditional exceedance for pairs at u = 0.8 and 0.9 and compare to the central-correlation Gaussian prediction.

interactions.mechanism: The relation between a goalie's saves leg and the game total leg is non-monotone: high pace lifts both, but a weak goalie lifts the total and lowers saves, so the sign of dependence depends on which latent factor drives the game.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress saves on total goals separately within bins of goalie save percentage shock and of opponent shot volume.

interactions.mechanism: The payoff after a void depends on the map; with nested or implied legs a void can make a leg redundant and change which legs are binding, so the effective probability depends jointly on the map and the logical relations.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute combo price under each candidate void map and flag combos for which the maps differ by more than a tick.

interactions.mechanism: Win and star shots legs are negatively linked only in the blowout regime where the leader's stars lose minutes; below a two-goal lead there is no link, so the dependence is a threshold in the lead.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the correlation between team win margin and star SOG for margins below two versus three or more.

nonlinearities.shape: Tail-dependent, stronger in the upper tail
nonlinearities.why: Combined events such as large win margin with high total with star points occur in a small set of high-scoring games, so joint exceedance probabilities grow faster than a constant correlation implies.

nonlinearities.shape: Hypothesised piecewise: star minutes may fall only beyond a two-goal margin (threshold to be estimated)
nonlinearities.why: Compression of stars' minutes appears in blowouts only, creating a kink in the relation between margin and star counts and a negative dependence regime absent in close games.

nonlinearities.shape: Error amplification across legs
nonlinearities.why: Probability errors on each leg multiply in an intersection, so a five percent relative error per leg becomes about 20 percent over four legs; the effect is multiplicative in log-probability, not additive.

contract.settlement_definition: Long-horizon contracts resolved on the official NHL regular season, playoffs or a named tournament: KXNHLPLAYOFF pays YES if the named team qualifies for the 2026-27 playoffs; KXNHLWEST/KXNHLEAST if it wins the 2026-27 conference final; KXNHL if it wins the 2026-27 Stanley Cup Finals; KXNHLSERIES if it wins a named playoff series (sampled: Montreal vs Buffalo 2026 2nd Round, historical market). KXNHLPRES pays if the team wins the Presidents' Trophy, ties in points broken by regulation wins, then regulation-plus-overtime wins, total wins, head-to-head points, goal differential and goals scored; KXNHLATLANTIC/METROPOLITAN/CENTRAL/PACIFIC pay if the team wins its division (no tiebreak text); KXNHLSEASONPTS pays if the team earns at least the stated standings points (e.g. 95, greater_or_equal), loser points included; KXNHLWSTREAK pays if the team has the longest regular-season winning streak, shared longest streaks paying $1/(number tied) rounded down; KXNHLRECORDWORST pays on the worst record after league tiebreaks, then dead heat 1/N. KXNHL4NATIONS (historical, finalized) paid if the named country won the 4 Nations Face-Off. Source of truth is the NHL's official standings, streak records and playoff/tournament results; no text addresses season or tournament cancellation.

rules_evidence.quote: If the Washington Capitals qualify for the playoffs in the 2026-27 NHL season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Playoff qualifier resolves on qualification under league rules (top three per division plus wild cards), so the tie-break rules and the points cut-off determine the boundary, and no secondary text defines it.

rules_evidence.quote: If the Winnipeg Jets win the 2026-27 NHL Western Conference Finals, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Conference champion pays on winning the Western Conference Finals, which requires qualifying and then winning three series (first round, second round and the final), so the contract mixes qualification, seed path and a three-series bracket.

rules_evidence.quote: official tie-breaking procedures will be applied until a single team remains
rules_evidence.establishes: Worst-record ties are broken by the league's official procedures until one team remains; the sampled text does not say which tiebreakers apply (sf4), so no regulation-win preference is claimed. It is a points-minimum event over 32 teams.

rules_evidence.quote: 1) Regulation wins 2) Regulation and overtime wins 3) Total wins 4) Head-to-head points
rules_evidence.establishes: Presidents' Trophy ties in points are broken by regulation wins first, so the simulation must track regulation, overtime and shootout wins separately, not just points.

rules_evidence.quote: official NHL standings points, awarded for wins and overtime or shootout losses in the 2026-27 NHL regular season
rules_evidence.establishes: The team points threshold counts loser points from extra-time losses, so the points pmf depends on the overtime rate and extra-time win share, not only on wins.

rules_evidence.quote: then the markets for each of those tied teams will resolve to $1/(the number of tied teams), rounded down
rules_evidence.establishes: Shared longest streaks pay 1/N, so the contract is an extremum-over-32-teams statistic with dead-heat payouts; the text does not say whether OT or shootout wins extend a streak.

rules_evidence.quote: If Washington Capitals wins the 2026-27 Stanley Cup® Finals, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The Cup contract is a plain outright on winning the Finals, i.e. qualification x four series wins along the realised bracket; no tiebreak, void or cancellation text.

rules_evidence.quote: win the Montreal Canadiens vs Buffalo Sabres 2nd Round series in the 2026 NHL playoffs
rules_evidence.establishes: The series-winner contract names a fixed matchup and round, so it is read off the best-of-seven recursion with the known home-ice order and the current series state.

rules_evidence.quote: If the Sweden wins the 4 Nations Face-Off, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: A national-team tournament outright: the outcome is generated by NHL-player national rosters in a short round robin plus final, not by club standings.

variants_and_edge_cases: Mixed mechanisms in one archetype: points thresholds (KXNHLSEASONPTS), argmax over a division or the league (division winners, Presidents' Trophy, worst record), qualification (KXNHLPLAYOFF), bracket outcomes (conference, Cup, series winner, exact final score) and a run-length extremum (KXNHLWSTREAK); each needs a different functional of the same season simulation.

Tiebreaks differ by contract: KXNHLPRES lists its own six-step order, KXNHLRECORDWORST defers to league procedures then 1/N, KXNHLWSTREAK pays 1/N with no tiebreak, and division contracts have no secondary text at all.

Rules text is now recovered for every series, but most are one sentence: KXNHL, KXNHLEAST, KXNHLWEST, KXNHLPLAYOFF, KXNHLSERIES and KXNHL4NATIONS say nothing about cancellation, a shortened season or a forfeited series.

Time horizon: markets trade for months, so information (injuries, trades at the deadline, goalie form) arrives with jumps, and a team eliminated from a race resolves its contracts early only in effect, not by rule.

KXNHL4NATIONS is a finalized historical market on the February 2025 best-on-best event (Canada, USA, Sweden, Finland); it is driven by national rosters and a three-game round robin plus a one-game final, and may not recur under this ticker.
KXNHLFINALSEXACT (exact Cup final score) was re-filed to unreg:playoff_series_aggregate and is no longer modelled here.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official NHL standings (points, RW, ROW), streak records and playoff bracket results.

mechanism.summary: A team future is the output of a two-layer simulation with uncertainty in the inputs. Layer one is the unknown team strength: posterior ratings from xG, goaltending and roster, with a drift and an uncertainty that matter as much as the mean because title odds are a convex function of rating. Layer two is the league mechanism: 82 games produce points through wins and overtime or shootout loser points; the playoff boundary is the 16th best record under division-and-wildcard rules with tiebreaks that favour regulation wins; the bracket then fixes opponents and home ice, and best-of-seven series amplify the variance of goaltending and injuries. The reassigned team counting contracts read other functionals of the same season simulation: a points threshold, the argmax of a division or of the league (Presidents' Trophy, with regulation-win tiebreaks), and the league-wide longest winning streak, a run-length extremum that depends on schedule sequence and streakiness rather than on totals. Settlement ties (dead heat, 1/N, tiebreakers) alter probabilities near the boundary. Information arrives slowly but with jumps (injuries, trades), so the posterior update is part of the price. A separate branch, the historical KXNHL4NATIONS outright, replaces team ratings with national-roster strength and the season simulation with a four-team round robin plus final.

stages.name: Team strength posterior with drift and uncertainty
stages.description: Each team's strength is a latent rating combining last season's performance, roster changes, age curves, goaltending and current-season xG, with weight on current data growing with games played (early November is about 14 games in). The posterior has an uncertainty of order 0.2 goals per game early in the year and follows a drift because of injuries and trades, so simulating with point ratings would overstate certainty and understate the probability of surprises.
stages.distribution: Gaussian-like posterior with sd 0.15-0.25 goals per game shrinking through the season, plus jump components for injuries and trades.

stages.name: Regular-season points accumulation and loser-point structure
stages.description: Remaining games are simulated with rest, travel, home and opponent strength; each game gives two points to the winner and one to an overtime or shootout loser, so a team's points include a loser-point stream that is partly skill and mostly noise. The points distribution across 82 games has sd about 7-8 points; the playoff cut-off sits near the mid-90s with its own uncertainty, and strength of schedule within division changes the remaining path.
stages.distribution: Sum of 82 game outcomes with 3-point structure (win in regulation 2, OT/SO win 2, OT/SO loss 1); points sd about 7-9; tiebreak counts (regulation wins) are a separate lattice.

stages.name: Qualification boundary, seeding and bracket path
stages.description: The top three teams in each division plus two wild cards per conference qualify; division winners face wild cards, so seeding determines opponent and home ice, and the same strength gives different championship odds by path. Tiebreakers (regulation wins first, then regulation-plus-overtime wins, then head-to-head etc.) decide close races, and a team's Cup probability depends on which seed it ends in and on rivals' seeds.
stages.distribution: Qualification is a threshold on a noisy points total; bracket path is a combinatorial function of the final standings with discrete seeds.

stages.name: Playoff series, goaltending variance and injuries
stages.description: Each series is best-of-seven with 2-2-1-1-1 home ice; the better team's single-game win probability is only 55-65 percent, so series are high variance, and goaltending hot streaks and injuries are large contributors beyond rating. The playoff environment changes penalty rates, depth usage and overtime format, and series state (games played, rest) updates probabilities. KXNHLSERIES (rules recovered: named matchup and round) is read directly off this recursion from the current series state, and KXNHLEAST/KXNHLWEST/KXNHL compose two to four such series along the bracket.
stages.distribution: Series win probability from best-of-seven recursion with single-game p near 0.55-0.62 and extra variance from goalie performance beyond binomial.

stages.name: Team counting, argmax and streak contracts
stages.description: KXNHLSEASONPTS, the four division winners, KXNHLPRES and KXNHLWSTREAK use the regular-season layer only. Each remaining game yields a regulation win, extra-time win or extra-time loss with probabilities from the rating posterior, so a team's points are banked points plus a compound sum with a loser-point stream. A threshold contract is the upper tail of that pmf; division and Presidents' Trophy contracts are argmax events over correlated totals, broken by regulation wins; KXNHLRECORDWORST is the argmin of the same correlated totals with league tiebreaks then a 1/N dead heat; the longest streak is the maximum run length over 32 teams, which depends on the order of home stands, back-to-backs and strong opponents and on any streakiness beyond strength.
stages.distribution: Points: near-Gaussian with sd about 7-9 for the remainder of the season; argmax events: categorical over a few contenders; streak maximum: geometric-type tail in run length with dead-heat mass at the top.

stages.name: National-team tournament outright (KXNHL4NATIONS)
stages.description: The 4 Nations Face-Off outcome is generated by four national rosters of NHL players, not by clubs. Each country's strength is the TOI-weighted value of its named skaters plus its starting goalie, minus injury withdrawals; the format is a single round robin (three games each) with standings points, then a one-game final between the top two. With only four games for the champion, the result is dominated by single-game variance and goaltending, and overtime/3v3 rules decide a large share of games. Win probability per game comes from the roster-strength gap through the same goal model used for club games.
stages.distribution: Categorical over four teams; per-game outcomes near 55-65 percent for the stronger side, so even a clear favourite rarely exceeds about 50 percent to win; heavy dependence on which goalie starts the final.

coaching_scheme.note: No input captures coach quality or in-season coaching changes as a driver of team strength and playoff performance; coaching change effects on ratings are unquantified and enter only through the news input.

officiating_rules.note: Playoff officiating tendencies (fewer calls, differing power-play counts) are only represented through the playoff context flag; there is no quantified input that translates officiating regime into series win probability.

nhl.rating_posterior_uncertainty.label: Team rating posterior uncertainty and in-season drift
nhl.rating_posterior_uncertainty.mechanism: Posterior standard deviation of each team's strength and its random-walk drift per game.
nhl.rating_posterior_uncertainty.rationale: A season or title simulation using point ratings is overconfident: the spread of true strengths and the error of the estimate both matter, and title probability is convex in rating so uncertainty raises the probability of mid-tier teams. Early-season data are noisy.
nhl.rating_posterior_uncertainty.measurement: Fit a state-space model: rating_t = rating_{t-1} + eta (sd 0.02 goals/game per game, estimated by out-of-sample likelihood), observation = score-adjusted xG differential and goal differential with measurement sd from game-level residuals; initialise with preseason prior (sd 0.25 goals/game). Output posterior mean and sd per team per day; draw ratings from the posterior in each simulation run. Re-estimate drift variance each season.
free_sources: Own computation from MoneyPuck/Natural Stat Trick game data
raw_data: team-game goals, xG, score effects, date; preseason projections
nhl.rating_posterior_uncertainty.why: Controls overconfidence in long-horizon contracts and is the main reason simple point ratings misprice the tails.

nhl.loser_point_rate.label: Loser-point and overtime-resolution rate by team
nhl.loser_point_rate.mechanism: Share of a team's games decided after regulation and its conditional win share.
nhl.loser_point_rate.rationale: Standings points include a point for an overtime or shootout loss, so two teams with equal win rates can differ in points by their extra-time frequency; regulation-win tiebreaks also depend on how often games are decided in regulation.
nhl.loser_point_rate.measurement: Per team and season compute: P(game goes beyond regulation) shrunk to league with k=30 games and 2-season weights; P(win | beyond regulation) shrunk to 0.5 with k=40 games (shootout/OT skill slight); regulation win rate from regulation results. Points per game = 2 x P(reg win) + 2 x P(extra) x p_win_extra + 1 x P(extra) x (1 - p_win_extra). Record regulation wins and ROW separately for tiebreak tracking.
raw_data: team-game result type (REG/OT/SO), points awarded, regulation wins
nhl.loser_point_rate.why: Maps game-level win probability into points and tiebreak counts, which the playoff boundary and Presidents' Trophy contracts depend on.

nhl.bracket_path_difficulty.label: Playoff bracket path difficulty by seed and division
nhl.bracket_path_difficulty.mechanism: Distribution of first and second round opponents and home-ice status given the final seed.
nhl.bracket_path_difficulty.rationale: The bracket pairs division winners with wild cards and keeps divisional paths, so equal-strength teams have different Cup and conference probabilities depending on their division and seed; the path must be simulated from standings.
nhl.bracket_path_difficulty.measurement: For each simulated final standings compute the bracket (3 per division plus 2 wild cards; division winner with better record faces the lower wild card) and the opponent set per round; record probabilities by team of facing each opponent and of home-ice in each series; use for series win recursion with rating uncertainty draws. Validate that simulated seed frequencies match historical qualifier frequencies by points.
raw_data: division membership, standings, format rules
nhl.bracket_path_difficulty.why: Turns qualification and seed into the opponent set that determines conference and Cup probability.

nhl.cap_flexibility_deadline.label: Cap flexibility and deadline additions capacity
nhl.cap_flexibility_deadline.mechanism: Cap space, long-term injured reserve relief and tradable assets that allow a team to add or replace players before the deadline.
nhl.cap_flexibility_deadline.rationale: A team's rating at the playoffs differs from today's rating through deadline moves and injury replacement; teams with cap room and assets can improve, which shifts long-horizon probabilities and is partially public.
nhl.cap_flexibility_deadline.measurement: From cap sites gather per team cap hit, projected deadline cap space (daily cap accrual x days remaining), LTIR usage, number of first-round picks and prospect capital (rank-based score from public prospect ratings); compute capacity = deadline space + LTIR relief; map to expected rating gain via historical deadline acquisitions of playoff contenders (average WAR added per cap dollar) with k=10 team-seasons; refresh weekly.
raw_data: team cap tables, LTIR status, pick inventory, trade logs
nhl.cap_flexibility_deadline.why: Adds a forward-looking component to ratings for contracts that resolve after the trade deadline.

nhl.series_goalie_volatility.label: Series-level goaltending volatility beyond binomial
nhl.series_goalie_volatility.mechanism: Extra variance of a series' save percentage and goal differential beyond a Bernoulli game model.
nhl.series_goalie_volatility.rationale: A best-of-seven series with fixed team ratings is binomial, but goalie performance autocorrelates within a series, producing a heavier-tailed distribution of series outcomes and more upsets than a constant p model gives.
nhl.series_goalie_volatility.measurement: From playoff series 2005-06 onward compute the series-level excess variance of goalie save percentage over binomial given shots faced; estimate intra-series correlation of single-game goalie GSAx; add a random effect on the winner's per-game p with sd estimated by maximum likelihood on series results; use in the series recursion. Shrink to league average with k=60 series.
raw_data: goalie-game shots, goals, GSAx; series outcomes
nhl.series_goalie_volatility.why: Short series are variance-dominated; this sets how far a rating gap translates to series win probability.

nhl.team_season_points_distribution.label: Team season points distribution (current points + remaining games with loser points)
nhl.team_season_points_distribution.mechanism: A team season point total is points banked plus the sum over remaining games of two points for a win and one for an overtime or shootout loss, so its distribution follows from per-game win and extra-time probabilities.
nhl.team_season_points_distribution.rationale: Six of the eight live series are team-level; a points threshold, a division title and a streak all need the same team-level layer: a rating posterior turned into per-game outcomes with the loser-point structure. This input states that chain explicitly rather than relying on undefined catalog items.
nhl.team_season_points_distribution.measurement: Per remaining game, P(regulation win), P(OT/SO win), P(OT/SO loss) from the team ratings posterior (score-adjusted xG differential plus goalie GSAx shrunk 1000 shots plus pdo regression, home and rest adjustments) with extra-time probability from the league tie model (about a quarter of games, to be measured); points = 2 x wins + 1 x extra-time losses; add points to date; simulate 20000 seasons drawing a rating from the posterior once per season; output the pmf of final points, P(points >= threshold) and the joint distribution across teams for the division winner using league tiebreaks (regulation wins first). As-of: standings and injuries as of the contract date.
free_sources: MoneyPuck team ratings and simulations (method reference)
raw_data: team-game results with regulation/OT/SO flags
team xG for and against by game
remaining schedule
nhl.team_season_points_distribution.why: Defines the points pmf behind KXNHLSEASONPTS, the four division-winner series and the Presidents' Trophy, all reassigned to this archetype.

nhl.schedule_sequence_profile.label: Schedule sequence profile (home stands, back-to-backs, opponent strength along the path)
nhl.schedule_sequence_profile.mechanism: Winning streaks and division races depend on the order of games, not only on their count: long home stands, runs of back-to-backs and strings of weak opponents raise the chance of long runs of wins.
nhl.schedule_sequence_profile.rationale: A longest-streak statistic is an extremum over 32 teams, so a small schedule-driven lift in the per-game win probability of a strong team over a stretch changes the tail. The same sequence matters for the remaining-schedule strength in a division race. The effect is small but is the only pregame-knowable driver of streak timing.
nhl.schedule_sequence_profile.measurement: For each team build the remaining game list with venue, rest days (back-to-back flag), travel and opponent rating (posterior mean); compute per-game win probability from the rating difference, home flag and rest effect and the cumulative win probability along every window of 8-20 games; output for each team the expected maximum run and the distribution of remaining-schedule strength; refresh daily. As-of: schedule is fixed in advance, ratings as of the contract date.
raw_data: team schedule with dates, venues and opponents
team ratings by date
rest and travel distance per game
nhl.schedule_sequence_profile.why: Supplies the remaining-schedule path (home stands, back-to-backs, opponent strength) that drives the longest-streak contract and close division races.

nhl.win_streak_extremum_dist.label: [Simulation output, not raw data] Winning-streak extremum distribution (league-wide max run length)
nhl.win_streak_extremum_dist.mechanism: Probability distribution of the longest winning streak among 32 teams over the season, and per-team shares.
nhl.win_streak_extremum_dist.rationale: The longest streak is an extremum, determined by the best teams' win probability and by streakiness; modelling teams one at a time with independent geometric runs underestimates the maximum when goalie form and schedule clusters create autocorrelation.
nhl.win_streak_extremum_dist.measurement: Simulate seasons from the rating posterior (with per-game win probabilities, drift and a goalie-form autocorrelation parameter estimated from historical runs: lag-1 correlation of results controlling for strength, k=600 games); for each simulation record each team's longest regular-season streak counting regulation, OT and shootout wins as wins unless the rules say otherwise; output per-team probability of holding the maximum (with 1/N for ties). Calibrate against 20 seasons of league-max streak lengths.
raw_data: team-game results with date, win flag, OT/SO flag
nhl.win_streak_extremum_dist.why: KXNHLWSTREAK pays on the league-wide longest regular-season winning streak, an extremum over 32 teams that no points model gives; model output, built from ratings and schedule.

nhl.national_team_roster_strength.label: National-team roster strength from NHL player values (best-on-best tournaments)
nhl.national_team_roster_strength.mechanism: A national team's goal differential per game is the sum of its players' individual contributions weighted by expected ice time, plus its starting goalie's save quality.
nhl.national_team_roster_strength.rationale: Club ratings cannot be reused: national rosters mix players from many clubs, depth is much higher than an NHL team's, and the decisive differences are the top-pair defence and the starting goalie; injury withdrawals after roster announcement move strength materially.
nhl.national_team_roster_strength.measurement: For each announced roster (as of the market timestamp): skater value = shrunk 3-season goals-above-replacement per 60 (or RAPM xGF-xGA per 60, k=1500 minutes shrinkage to positional mean), multiplied by projected TOI share from the announced lines (top-6 F ~17 min, D1 ~23 min); goalie value = 3-season GSAx per 60 shrunk with k=3000 shots; team value = sum skaters + expected starter value; convert to per-game goal differential with the club goal model; recompute on each withdrawal or replacement.
free_sources: MoneyPuck and Natural Stat Trick player stats
raw_data: national roster lists with announcement and withdrawal dates
player GAR/RAPM or xGF/xGA on-ice per 60, TOI
goalie shots against and GSAx
nhl.national_team_roster_strength.why: KXNHL4NATIONS settles on which country wins the tournament; national-roster strength is the only talent input that generates that outcome.

nhl.short_tournament_format_sim.label: Short best-on-best tournament format simulation (round robin plus final)
nhl.short_tournament_format_sim.mechanism: The champion is determined by a three-game round robin with standings points and tiebreaks, then one final game, so the title probability is a functional of per-game win probabilities under the format.
nhl.short_tournament_format_sim.rationale: Four games make the outcome variance-dominated; the points system (regulation vs overtime wins), the round-robin tiebreak and overtime rules change which two teams reach the final, so a simple strength ranking overstates the favourite.
nhl.short_tournament_format_sim.measurement: Monte Carlo (20000 draws): for each scheduled round-robin game draw regulation result from the bivariate goal model of the two roster strengths with a home-crowd term for the host nation, resolve ties by the published OT/shootout format, award standings points per the published scheme, rank with published tiebreakers, play the final with the tournament's overtime rule; output P(win) per country as of the market timestamp, updated after each played game.
free_sources: NHL API game results for completed tournament games
raw_data: tournament schedule, venues, points scheme, tiebreak order, OT/shootout format
completed game results
nhl.short_tournament_format_sim.why: Maps national-roster strength into the KXNHL4NATIONS outright; without the format the probabilities of finalists and champion are miscalibrated.

nhl.ratings.reason: Central object, but the label bundles inputs with the simulation procedure; the rating needs a posterior with drift and uncertainty, which is added separately.

nhl.xg_for.reason: Offensive component of the rating; useful as an ingredient, not a separate predictor beyond the rating.

nhl.xg_against.reason: Defensive component of the rating; same role as xg_for and should enter jointly with goaltending.

nhl.goalie_quality.reason: Largest single-player component of team strength especially in the playoffs, but GSAx persistence is low so shrinkage is essential.

nhl.injuries_pit.reason: Long-term injuries to key players change strength for months; the contract effect depends on replacement capacity, not the flag alone.

nhl.pdo_regression.reason: Regresses lucky standings before simulation; useful early in the season when records are driven by luck.

nhl.sos_remaining.reason: Remaining schedule changes points expectations modestly and matters only near the boundary of qualification.

nhl.standings_tiebreakers.reason: Regulation-win tiebreaks decide boundary and Presidents' Trophy ties and require tracking of regulation wins in the simulation.

nhl.series_context.reason: Needed for KXNHLSERIES (reassigned here, no listed markets yet) and for in-playoff updating of conference and Cup contracts; in November no series is underway, so it carries no information until April.

nhl.playoff_context.reason: Changes environment and format parameters of series simulation; a regime flag rather than a team feature.

nhl.news.reason: Trades and coaching changes shift strength after ratings are fitted; unstructured, so it is useful only after being converted to rating changes.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook futures prices are a benchmark for comparison; using them as input contaminates a fundamentals-based forecast.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi's own price path reflects market beliefs; it is useful for studying news reaction, not as a causal input.

nhl.season_sim_distribution.reason: The ratings label already includes season simulation; the simulation is a procedure applied to ratings and tiebreak rules, not a separate input.

nhl.award_vote_share_model.reason: The voted award series (Hart, Norris, Vezina, Calder, Lindsay) were reassigned to season_awards_and_stats, which now carries this vote model; no team future here resolves by vote.

nhl.award_eligibility_tiebreak_map.reason: Award eligibility and the Art Ross/Richard tiebreak matter only to the award and stat-title series, which the final series assignment moved to season_awards_and_stats.

nhl.player_season_points_projection.reason: Player points projection serves Art Ross/Hart (season_awards_and_stats) and season player points (season-counting archetype); no team future in this archetype uses an individual total.

nhl.goalie_award_projection.reason: Vezina projection belongs to the goalie award, now in season_awards_and_stats; team goaltending enters team futures through goalie_quality and series_goalie_volatility instead.

nhl.rookie_role_pedigree.reason: Calder-only prior; the Calder series was reassigned to season_awards_and_stats, so no contract here uses rookie pedigree.

interactions.mechanism: Title probability is a convex function of team rating, so rating uncertainty raises the probability of mid-tier teams and lowers that of favourites relative to a point-rating simulation; the effect is strongest early in the season and fades as the posterior tightens.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate with and without rating draws and compare Cup probabilities by seed and across horizons.

interactions.mechanism: A seven-game series amplifies single-game randomness and goalie volatility compounds with series length: the same rating gap yields a lower win probability than a constant-p recursion would give once goalie autocorrelation is included.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit series outcomes with and without a random goalie effect and compare upset frequency.

interactions.mechanism: Regulation wins are the first tiebreaker, so two teams with equal points but different loser-point counts have different qualification odds; the effect arises only at ties and is conditional on the points boundary.
interactions.how_to_test: Count playoff outcomes of tied-on-points teams by regulation wins over history and compare with a points-only model.

interactions.mechanism: A long-term injury to a key player reduces rating, but a team with cap space and assets can replace part of the loss before the deadline, so the effect on a futures price is conditional on capacity and on the date of the injury.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare change in end-of-season rating after star injuries for teams with high and low capacity.

interactions.mechanism: Seed and division create path differences: a division winner plays a wild card while the other seeds meet inside the division; at the boundary between third seed and wild card, the path regime switches, so marginal points have an outsized effect on conference and Cup odds.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute conference and Cup probabilities for the same rating under each of the possible seed placements and compare.

interactions.mechanism: A long winning run needs a strong team AND a soft stretch of schedule (home stand, few back-to-backs, weak opponents); because the league maximum is driven by the single best realised run, rating uncertainty and an easy schedule window multiply in the tail, so a mid-strength team with a long soft stretch can out-price a stronger team with a balanced schedule.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate league-max streaks with real schedules versus shuffled schedules at the same ratings, and compare both to 20 seasons of observed league-max streak lengths and holders.

interactions.mechanism: In a four-game tournament the starting goalie's save quality multiplies the effect of skater depth: a deep skater roster with a weak starter loses much of its edge because a single elimination-style final is decided on few goals, so goalie quality carries more weight than in an 82-game season.
interactions.how_to_test: Across historical best-on-best tournaments (Olympics with NHL players, World Cups, 4 Nations), compare champion prediction with skater-only vs skater-plus-goalie strength.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in rating for championship probability
nonlinearities.why: Winning four best-of-seven rounds multiplies four probabilities, so a small rating advantage compounds; the title odds of the top team rise faster than linearly with rating and the odds of weak qualifiers fall faster than linearly.

nonlinearities.shape: Logistic around the playoff points cut-off
nonlinearities.why: Qualification is a threshold event: the probability moves from near zero to near one over a range of about 10-15 points around the mid-90s cut-off, so small changes in expected points matter most for bubble teams.

nonlinearities.shape: Decreasing in games played
nonlinearities.why: Posterior sd of rating falls roughly with the inverse square root of games played plus a drift floor, so the uncertainty premium for long-horizon futures is largest now and decays through the season.
