contract.settlement_definition: Each series pays YES if the named person wins the named 2026-27 NHL award: voted awards KXNHLHART (and its title-only duplicate KXNHLMVP), KXNHLNORRIS, KXNHLCALDER, KXNHLVEZINA, KXNHLLINDSAY (player-voted) and KXNHLADAMS (coach), and statistic-decided trophies KXNHLROSS (points leader) and KXNHLRICHARD (goals leader). Where the secondary text is sampled (Adams, Calder, Lindsay, Norris, Richard, Ross, Vezina), a tie for the award pays Yes $1/N rounded down to the cent and No $1 minus that; the sampled Hart text carries no tie clause. Settlement follows the league's announced winner, so whether a league tiebreak (Art Ross) precedes the 1/N rule is not stated. KXNHLPLAYOFFGOALS (historical, 'Playoffs Goal Leader (by Round)') pays YES if the named player records the most goals in the specified playoff round (sampled: the 2026 Stanley Cup Finals); a player who enters no game of that round resolves at a fair market price, and tied leaders pay $1/N rounded down.

rules_evidence.quote: If Todd McLellan wins the NHL Jack Adams Award in the 2026-27 NHL season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The contract resolves on the league's announced winner of the Jack Adams Award for the 2026-27 season; the winner is chosen by voters, so no statistic settles it.

rules_evidence.quote: positions will pay $1/N (rounded down to the nearest cent), where N is the number of tied participants
rules_evidence.establishes: The Art Ross contract pays 1/N on a tie for the award; since the league names one Art Ross winner via its own tiebreak, the 1/N clause binds only if the league itself declares a shared award, which is unverified (aw10).

rules_evidence.quote: If William Nylander wins the NHL Ted Lindsay Award in the 2026-27 NHL season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The Lindsay contract settles on the announced winner of a player-voted award, so its electorate (players, not writers) and the absence of published vote shares (aw8) shape the model.

rules_evidence.quote: If Alexis Lafreniere wins the NHL Hart Memorial Trophy in the 2026-27 NHL season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Hart settles on the announced MVP winner; the sampled secondary text contains only a non-affiliation notice and no tie clause, unlike the other award series.

rules_evidence.quote: If a player does not enter any game during the Stanley Cup Finals®, the market for that player will resolve to a fair market price.
rules_evidence.establishes: The round goal-leader contract conditions on the player appearing in the round; with only 4-7 games and leaders often on 3-5 goals, the 1/N tie clause in the same text is frequently binding.

variants_and_edge_cases: Voted versus counted: Hart, Norris, Calder and Vezina are decided by voters (writers; general managers for Vezina), Lindsay by players, Jack Adams by broadcasters (to be verified, aw2), while Art Ross and Rocket Richard go to the statistical leader, so two different generating processes share this archetype.

Ties: Rocket Richard has been shared when players tied in goals, so the 1/N clause is live for it; Art Ross uses a league tiebreak (more goals first, from memory) so a shared award is rare; voted-award ties are rare; the sampled Hart text has no tie clause at all.
Coach award: a head coach can be fired or replaced mid-season, a case the sampled text does not address (interim coaches' eligibility unspecified).

Timing: ballots for voted awards are cast at the end of the regular season and winners announced weeks later, so playoff results do not matter, while stat titles are fixed at the last regular-season game.
KXNHLMVP is a title-only duplicate of KXNHLHART with no listed markets; if it lists, it must be priced identically to Hart for the same player.

KXNHLPLAYOFFGOALS is a round-specific playoff goal-leader contract (sampled on the 2026 Finals, historical): the candidate pool is the two finalists' rosters, exposure is the unknown series length, and multi-way ties at the top are common, so 1/N settlement is a large part of the payoff.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official NHL award announcements (league and voting bodies, NHLPA for Lindsay) and official NHL regular-season statistics for Art Ross and Rocket Richard.

mechanism.summary: These contracts resolve through two processes. Voted awards (Hart, Norris, Calder, Vezina, Lindsay, Jack Adams) are a choice by an electorate over a few candidates: each candidate's projected end-of-season line (points, goals, ice time, goalie save quality and starts, rookie role) plus team success and narrative feeds a vote model, and coaches are judged on results versus expectation. Statistic-decided trophies (Art Ross, Rocket Richard) go to the league leader in points or goals, so the probability is the chance a player's random season total exceeds every rival's, which depends on rate, games played and the common league scoring level. Ballot deadlines, finalist announcements and injuries make step changes in information, and tie rules (1/N, league tiebreaks, shared Richard) matter near the top. A third process, the round-specific KXNHLPLAYOFFGOALS contract, is a short-horizon leaderboard: the maximum of goal counts over the rosters still playing in that round, with series length as common exposure and frequent 1/N ties.

stages.name: Candidate pool and eligibility
stages.description: For each award the candidate pool is defined by eligibility and realistic contention: every head coach in office for the Jack Adams, rookies meeting the age and prior-games limits for the Calder, defencemen for the Norris, goalies for the Vezina, all skaters for Hart, Lindsay and the stat titles. Mid-season firings, injuries and trades change the pool, and early in the season the realistic pool is still wide, so the probability mass outside the top five candidates is material.
stages.distribution: Short list of 3-6 serious candidates with heavy-tailed probabilities; the remaining candidates share a small residual.

stages.name: Performance relative to expectation (coaching award)
stages.description: The award rewards over-performance: realised points percentage minus what a preseason projection predicted, the year-over-year change, and whether the team did it despite injuries or roster loss. Team strength estimates and their uncertainty determine the expected result; the outcome distribution of final points is wide (sd of 7-9 points), so a leader in November is only mildly informative about the final ranking of coaches.
stages.distribution: Final points of each team ~ Gaussian around the projection with sd 7-9; the coach ranking is the ranking of expectation gaps, so the maximum of many noisy gaps.

stages.name: Electorate, ballot timing and narrative
stages.description: Voters weigh narrative as much as the numbers: first-year coaches, turnarounds and managing through injuries; the electorate (a specific broadcasters' association, to be verified) casts ballots at the end of the regular season, so what happens in the playoffs is irrelevant and the finalist list narrows to three. Award timing introduces step changes in information when finalists are named.
stages.distribution: Multinomial choice over finalists with a few candidates holding most mass; vote shares typically spread across 3 finalists.

stages.name: Voted player awards (Hart/MVP, Norris, Calder, Vezina, Lindsay)
stages.description: Each voted player award is a vote model applied to a projected season line: skaters through points projection, ice time and power-play role, defencemen additionally through usage for the Norris, goalies through GSAx rate and starts share for the Vezina, rookies through role and pedigree for the Calder. Writers reward team success for the Hart, general managers vote the Vezina and players vote the Lindsay, whose vote shares are not known to be published, so its model rests on finalists and winners only. Missing games pushes a candidate out of contention in steps rather than linearly.
stages.distribution: Multinomial over a small candidate set with heavy-tailed vote shares; each candidate projection is a rate times games distribution with an injury left tail.

stages.name: Statistic-decided leaders (Art Ross, Rocket Richard)
stages.description: Art Ross and Rocket Richard pay the player with the most regular-season points or goals, so a contender's probability is the share of simulated seasons in which his banked total plus a random rest-of-season count beats every rival's. All contenders must be simulated jointly: the league scoring level shifts everyone together and largely cancels, while games missed and individual rate uncertainty decide the leader. Richard is goals-only (shot volume times shooting talent), Ross is points; ties at the top are resolved by the league tiebreak for Ross and by a shared award for Richard.
stages.distribution: Leader identity: categorical over 3-8 contenders from the maximum of correlated compound counts; tie mass at the top of order a few percent for goals, smaller for points.

stages.name: Playoff-round goal leader (KXNHLPLAYOFFGOALS)
stages.description: For a single playoff round the goal leader is the player with the most goals across that series (for the Finals, two rosters only). Each skater's goals are his per-game goal rate (shots x finishing x opposing goalie, PP role) times the number of games he plays, and the number of games is the shared, random series length (4-7) that scales every candidate together; injuries and lineup changes during the series alter exposure. With low totals, ties at the maximum are frequent and settle 1/N, while a player not dressing for any game is settled at fair price.
stages.distribution: Per-player goals are overdispersed Poisson-gamma over 4-7 games (leaders typically 3-5); the maximum over roughly 36 skaters has large tie mass, so the payoff distribution includes fractional 1/N outcomes.

game_context_script.note: Single-game scripts average out over a season; team success, which voters reward, enters through nhl.ratings and the coach expectation delta rather than through any within-game state.

opponent_matchup.note: All contracts resolve on season-long totals or votes; opponents average out over 82 games and no pairing between teams or players decides any of them.

environment.note: Rink, weather and travel conditions have no direct effect on a coach vote or a draft selection beyond their small influence on team results, which the ratings already contain.

pace_volume.note: Rate times games and ice time drive the stat-title races and skater award projections.

efficiency_conversion.note: Goalie GSAx and skater finishing convert volume into the goals and save numbers that decide Richard and Vezina.

officiating_rules.note: Officiating has no direct bearing on a vote or a season leaderboard beyond power-play volume already inside the player projections; the rule-like elements are eligibility and tiebreaks, handled as settlement inputs.

nhl.coach_expectation_delta.label: Coach expectation delta (results versus preseason projection, year-over-year change)
nhl.coach_expectation_delta.mechanism: Difference between realised points percentage and the preseason-projected value, plus year-over-year change and coaching tenure flags.
nhl.coach_expectation_delta.rationale: The Jack Adams Award is voted on who coached best relative to expectations, so what matters is the surprise, not the level; a team that finished first as expected earns less credit than one that jumped from the bottom. The expectation must be formed before the season to avoid hindsight bias.
nhl.coach_expectation_delta.measurement: Preseason projection P_exp = last two seasons' points percentage blend (0.6/0.4) adjusted by roster change impact and age; delta = realised points pct to date (or simulated final) minus P_exp, with standard error from remaining games; add change from last season, first-year-coach flag, injury games lost to key players, and goalie change flag. Fit a ranking model of historical winners/finalists on delta and these flags (20 seasons) and output candidate win probabilities with simulation draws for final points.
raw_data: team season points pct, preseason projections, coach tenure, injury games lost
nhl.coach_expectation_delta.why: The core of the Jack Adams voter model and absent from the draft's player-production inputs.

nhl.player_season_points_projection.label: Player season points projection (rate x games-played distribution)
nhl.player_season_points_projection.mechanism: A season points threshold is reached by points already banked plus per-game production on the games still to be played, so the outcome is the sum of a rate (role, time on ice, power-play share, on-ice chance creation and credit share) and an opportunity count (games played).
nhl.player_season_points_projection.rationale: Season-points contracts such as a 110+ points threshold for a defenceman sit in the extreme tail of a rate times games distribution, so both the central rate and its dispersion matter. Rate comes from the same components as the single-game record (role, power-play time, on-ice xGF, individual points percentage); games remaining comes from the games-played hazard. The subtle part is that role changes (power-play unit, line, injuries to teammates) move the rate level for the rest of the season.
nhl.player_season_points_projection.measurement: Points to date P0 plus the sum over remaining games g of expected points per game, where per-game expected points = sum over strength states of (on-ice goals-for per 60 x projected state time on ice per 60 x individual points percentage in that state), using 3 seasons weighted 0.5/0.3/0.2 with half-life 1.5 seasons, shrunk to position-and-role priors (k=25 on-ice goals) and updated for the current season by a gamma-Poisson rate posterior; multiply by the pmf of games remaining from nhl.games_played_hazard; simulate 20000 seasons with negative-binomial per-game dispersion fitted on player-seasons of comparable rate; report P(total >= threshold). As-of: all games before the contract date, with the current power-play unit and line assignment from the latest lineup report.
free_sources: NHL API player game logs and play-by-play (api-web.nhle.com)
raw_data: player-game goals, assists, time on ice by strength state
on-ice goals-for per strength state
games-played and injury history per player-season
nhl.player_season_points_projection.why: Gives the season-points contracts a market-free chain (rate, role, games played) instead of leaving them to a single-game or goals-only mechanism.

nhl.goalie_award_projection.label: Goalie award projection (Vezina: GSAx rate, starts share, team context)
nhl.goalie_award_projection.mechanism: A goalie award is decided on saves above expectation and workload over the season, so the rest-of-season distribution is the goalie rate (GSAx per start, save percentage) times the number of starts he gets, with the team context that shapes the voters narrative.
nhl.goalie_award_projection.rationale: Vezina voters (general managers) reward workload and results; a goalie who splits starts cannot accumulate the case of a clear number one, and GSAx has low persistence so the projection must be shrunk heavily. The subtle part is starts share: it is set by the team depth chart and back-to-back schedule, not only by quality.
nhl.goalie_award_projection.measurement: Per goalie: GSAx per 60 over 3 seasons weighted 0.5/0.3/0.2 shrunk toward the league mean with k=1500 shots faced; projected remaining starts = games remaining x starts share (team goalie rotation pattern, back-to-back share, 2-season average, shrunk to 0.6 for a clear number one); simulate remaining GSAx as normal with sd from shots-faced noise; add wins and save percentage to date. As-of: all games before the contract date, current depth chart from the latest lineup reports.
raw_data: goalie-game shots faced, goals against, xG against, starter flag
team goalie rotation and schedule
nhl.goalie_award_projection.why: Gives the Vezina contract a goalie-specific production chain (rate, starts share, shrinkage) that skater inputs do not provide.

nhl.rookie_role_pedigree.label: Rookie role and pedigree for Calder candidates
nhl.rookie_role_pedigree.mechanism: Calder voters pick the best first-year player, so the probability depends on eligibility, the rookie role actually obtained (line, power-play unit, minutes) and the production pace, with pedigree (draft position, prior league) setting early expectations.
nhl.rookie_role_pedigree.rationale: A rookie projection has little NHL history, so draft slot, junior or college scoring and age carry weight early while deployment (top-six, PP1, defence pair) dominates once games are played. Eligibility rules (age cap, prior games) also remove candidates, which makes the candidate set itself uncertain.
nhl.rookie_role_pedigree.measurement: Prior points per game = league translation factor for the prior league (CHL, NCAA, European) applied to the last season points per game, regressed 50 percent toward the draft-slot mean; posterior update with NHL games to date by gamma-Poisson with prior weight equal to 20 games; add role terms (share of team forward TOI, PP1 flag) and eligibility flag from the league rulebook; output rest-of-season points projection and eligibility probability. As-of: before each ballot deadline.
free_sources: Elite Prospects player pages (draft and prior-league stats)
raw_data: prior-league player-season stats
draft slot and age
NHL player-game TOI by strength state
nhl.rookie_role_pedigree.why: Supplies the rookie-specific prior and role inputs for the Calder contract that veteran production inputs lack.

nhl.award_vote_share_model.label: Award vote-share model (electorate-specific)
nhl.award_vote_share_model.mechanism: Historical multinomial-logit model of vote shares for each award using production, team success, position and narrative variables.
nhl.award_vote_share_model.rationale: Hart, Norris and Calder are voted by writers and Vezina by general managers; each electorate rewards different features (points, team rank, goalie wins, shutouts, GSAx), so a single player-quality model does not map to voting outcomes.
nhl.award_vote_share_model.measurement: For each award collect the last 20 seasons' finalists and vote shares; regress log vote share on points per game, goals, team points percentage, games played, position and for goalies wins, save percentage and shutouts; fit multinomial logit with season fixed effects and shrinkage; apply to the projected end-of-season stat line distribution from simulations; output win probability by candidate with draw uncertainty; update with finalists and ballot dates. Source caveat (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for the Ted Lindsay Award): full vote shares are not known to be published for player-voted awards (only finalists and the winner), so where shares are missing fit a conditional-logit on winner-among-finalists instead of a share regression; with only a few dozen finalists per award use at most 4 covariates and strong shrinkage.
raw_data: award voting results with candidates, vote points, season stats
nhl.award_vote_share_model.why: Needed for the six award and stat title contracts because they resolve by voters, not by team quality.

nhl.playoff_round_goal_leader_sim.label: Playoff-round goal-leader simulation (series length x per-game goal rates, tie mass)
nhl.playoff_round_goal_leader_sim.mechanism: The round leader is the argmax of goal counts accumulated over a random number of games by the skaters of the teams in that round, with ties split 1/N.
nhl.playoff_round_goal_leader_sim.rationale: Season leaderboard inputs do not transfer: exposure is a 4-7 game series common to all candidates, opponents are fixed (one goalie dominates conversion), playoff PP rates differ, and with leaders on 3-5 goals ties are common, so the fair price is an expectation over fractional payouts rather than a simple max probability.
nhl.playoff_round_goal_leader_sim.measurement: As of the market timestamp: per game, each skater's goal rate = shrunk playoff+regular ixG/60 x finishing factor (k=150 shots) x projected TOI by state x opposing starter's GSAx adjustment; series-length pmf from per-game win probabilities with the 2-2-1-1-1 home pattern and current series state; simulate 20000 series drawing lineup availability per game, count goals, compute each player's expected payout = sum over sims of 1{max}/N_tied; players who appear in no game are excluded (fair-price leg).
raw_data: playoff and regular-season player shots, ixG, goals, TOI by state
series schedule and state
starting goalie per game
nhl.playoff_round_goal_leader_sim.why: KXNHLPLAYOFFGOALS pays on the round's goal leader with 1/N ties; this simulation is the only input producing that functional.

nhl.award_stats.reason: Its measurement bundles a rest-of-season rate x games projection (now defined exactly by player_season_points_projection and goalie_award_projection) with a voter-score regression (award_vote_share_model); keeping it alongside both double-counts the same quantities.

nhl.award_voting_rules.reason: The electorate, ballot timing and finalists define when information can matter; needs the Jack Adams voting body and timing verified.

nhl.toi_trend.reason: Irrelevant to the coach award and draft, but recent role changes (ice time, power-play promotion) move a skater award candidate rest-of-season projection; kept for the player-award series re-mapped here.

nhl.pp_role.reason: Power-play unit share drives points for Norris and Hart candidates; irrelevant to the coach award and draft but needed for the player-award series re-mapped here.

nhl.ixg_player.reason: Now primary: Rocket Richard was reassigned here, and the goals leader is decided by individual goal rate, whose most stable component is ixG per 60; also separates scoring talent from luck for Hart candidates.

nhl.finishing.reason: Shrunk shooting talent layered on ixG for the Rocket Richard leader race (reassigned here); small persistent effect, but over a season it moves a 50-goal pace by a few goals.

nhl.goalie_quality.reason: Component of team rating for the coach delta and the primary driver of the Vezina goalie projection (nhl.goalie_award_projection) for the re-mapped goalie award.

nhl.career_trajectory.reason: Age curve does not map to a coach vote, but it anchors Calder and ageing-star projections and draft prospect development; kept for the re-mapped player awards and draft.

nhl.injuries_pit.reason: Injuries to key players set the expectation against which the coach is judged and can create an adversity narrative.

nhl.ratings.reason: Team strength and the standing relative to preseason expectation underlie the coach vote and set the lottery odds, but the entry must combine it with the expectation delta.

nhl.announcement_calendar.reason: Ballot, finalist and draft dates determine which information is incorporated; useful as a timing mask.

nhl.news.reason: Coach firings, trades and eligibility news change the candidate set; unstructured and sparse.

nhl.stat_dist.reason: Single-game count shapes are not what these contracts depend on; season totals for the stat titles use the compound season count inside player_season_points_projection, so this per-game input adds nothing.

nhl.draft_lottery_odds_by_standing.reason: Defined for KXNHLDRAFTTOP/KXNHLDRAFTPICK, which the final series assignment moved to unreg:draft_selection; no award or stat-title series in this archetype depends on the draft chain.

nhl.pick_ownership_and_protection.reason: Defined for KXNHLDRAFTTOP/KXNHLDRAFTPICK, which the final series assignment moved to unreg:draft_selection; no award or stat-title series in this archetype depends on the draft chain.

nhl.prospect_consensus_ranking.reason: Defined for KXNHLDRAFTTOP/KXNHLDRAFTPICK, which the final series assignment moved to unreg:draft_selection; no award or stat-title series in this archetype depends on the draft chain.

interactions.mechanism: A coach's vote probability depends on over-performance conditional on adversity: a team beating projection while missing top players is valued above the same delta with a healthy roster, so injuries amplify the narrative only when the team is still above expectation.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit historical finalists on delta with an interaction with injury games lost and check coefficient sign.

interactions.mechanism: Information after the ballot deadline cannot change the vote, so the effect of late-season form on the award is zero beyond the cut-off date, whereas before it each point of final points shifts candidate probabilities; the timing creates a threshold in the usefulness of data.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare award outcomes against standings at the ballot date versus at season end across 15 seasons.

interactions.mechanism: The Art Ross leader is the maximum over correlated contenders: the league scoring level multiplies every contender and largely cancels in who leads, while games missed are idiosyncratic, so a two-week injury to the favourite transfers probability to the next contenders far more than a league-wide scoring drop does.
interactions.how_to_test: Back-test leader probabilities with and without the common league factor and with games-played uncertainty switched off, scoring the Ross and Richard winners of past seasons.

interactions.mechanism: Hart voters rarely pick a player whose team misses the playoffs, so for equal projected points the win probability is much lower below the playoff line; the team-strength effect acts as a gate on the candidate, not as an additive bonus.
interactions.how_to_test: In 20 seasons of Hart voting regress vote share on points with an interaction for team playoff qualification and compare with an additive model.

interactions.mechanism: General managers voting the Vezina weight wins and save percentage, which depend on team defence and starts share as well as on goalie skill, so a strong goalie behind a weak defence or in a tandem is under-rewarded relative to his GSAx; the effect of GSAx on vote share is conditional on starts and team results.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress Vezina vote share on GSAx, starts and team points percentage with interactions over 15 seasons and compare with GSAx alone.

interactions.mechanism: Series length is a common exposure that raises every candidate's expected goals together, but a longer series also increases the spread between top scorers and reduces tie probability, so the favourite's payout gains less from extra games than his count suggests while 1/N splits shrink.
interactions.how_to_test: In historical playoff rounds, regress the number of tied leaders and the leader's goal count on series length.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold for finalist selection
nonlinearities.why: A coach with a delta below roughly one to two standard errors of the leaders is rarely among the three finalists, so the vote probability is near zero below a threshold and rises steeply above it.

nonlinearities.shape: Logistic in the projected gap to the nearest rival
nonlinearities.why: Leader probability for Art Ross is a smooth step in the projected points gap whose width is set by rest-of-season sd; once a contender leads by more than about two sds late in the season the probability saturates near one.

nonlinearities.shape: Winner-take-most: convex in vote-score lead
nonlinearities.why: Win probability depends on the candidate's rank in a multinomial over a few finalists, so small leads in the voter score translate into large win-probability gaps once the field narrows.

contract.settlement_definition: Four unrelated event types share this archetype. KXNHLNEXTTEAM pays YES for the named team if it is the player's next team before the stated date (the sample is 'before Nov 1, 2026'); a player who retires or has no team resolves a 'Retires / No Team' contract, a player who remains on his issuance team resolves that team, and signing with any team including the previous one after free agency counts. KXNHLEXPANSION pays YES if the NHL officially announces an expansion franchise award to a named city before Jan 1, 2027, requiring formal approval naming the city. KXNHLRETIRE (historical) pays YES if the named player announces his NHL retirement before the stated season start date, the retirement intended to be effective immediately or before the next season. KXNHLNEXTGM (historical) pays YES for the named person if he is appointed, elected, named, designated or succeeded to the named team's General Manager position before the stated date (sample: Toronto, before Nov 1, 2026). Neither text addresses interim titles or later reversals.

rules_evidence.quote: The league must officially announce that the city has been awarded an expansion franchise.
rules_evidence.establishes: Resolution needs an official league announcement of a franchise award; reports, stadium approvals and feasibility studies do not count, so insider reports are not settlement events.

rules_evidence.quote: If Quinn Hughes remains on the team they were on upon issuance on Nov 1, 2026, then the market for that team will resolve Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Staying put resolves the incumbent team's market, so the default outcome is the status quo and the contract is about the probability of a change of team inside the window.

rules_evidence.quote: the retirement must be intended to be effective immediately or prior to the first new season after the announcement
rules_evidence.establishes: A farewell-tour announcement effective after the coming season does not qualify; only an announcement taking effect before the next season counts, and it must come before the season start date.

rules_evidence.quote: is appointed, elected, named, designated, or succeeded to the position as General Manager for Toronto Maple Leafs
rules_evidence.establishes: Any form of naming to the GM title settles YES for that person, so a multi-outcome partition over candidates; the text does not say whether an interim or acting GM title counts.

variants_and_edge_cases: Four different generating processes: a transaction destination (partition over 32 teams plus retire/no team), a governance event (expansion approval by the Board of Governors), a personal career decision (retirement announcement before a season) and a front-office hire (partition over GM candidates), so no single base rate covers them.

Next-team window: the sampled market is 'before Nov 1, 2026', a date already passed on the review date (Nov 7, 2026), so the sample is stale or expired; the text 'is a free agent ... for any period of time' means a re-signing with the same team counts as YES for that team after free agency.
Expansion contract requires the announcement to come after market issuance and to name the city; relocation counts only if designated expansion, and the team need not begin play before the date.

KXNHLRETIRE: an announcement effective after the next season (a farewell season) does not count; KXNHLNEXTGM: 'designated' or 'succeeded' is broad enough that an interim appointment might settle YES, which the text does not resolve.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official NHL and NHLPA announcements for awards and expansion; NHL transaction records for next team.

mechanism.summary: These markets are not produced by on-ice play; they are produced by institutions with calendars, constraints and information channels. For a destination market the outcome is a draw from a discrete set of teams constrained by the player's contract status (expiry year, no-move clauses, signing windows), by the cap space and needs of potential suitors, and by the time window; the default is the status quo and the main hazard is concentrated at a few calendar points. For a governance event like expansion the outcome requires a formal board decision after preparatory steps (city readiness, ownership, arena, fee, announced timeline), so the event is gated by the calendar of meetings. In all cases information arrives through insider reports that are informative but not settling events, so the model must weight credibility and lag between report and official announcement. Retirement and GM-hire markets add two person-level processes: an age- and contract-driven retirement hazard before a season deadline, and a candidate choice by a club's leadership once a GM vacancy exists.

stages.name: Event class and reference-class hazard
stages.description: Each contract is first placed in a reference class with its own base rate: a star defenceman changing teams within a given window, a league expanding within a year, a veteran of a given age and contract status retiring before a season, a vacant GM chair being filled by a given candidate type. The reference class must be narrow because pooling destination, governance and voting events gives meaningless base rates. The hazard inside the window depends on how many calendar events fall within it.
stages.distribution: Rare event with a time-varying hazard; for destination markets the base probability of a move inside a short window is a few percent for incumbents under contract and high for free agents at the market open.

stages.name: Institutional gates and constraints
stages.description: A player can only move if his contract allows it: expiry, no-trade and no-move lists, signing windows and arbitration status define the set of feasible destinations; suitors need cap space and roster room. An expansion award needs a Board of Governors approval after an expansion process, which is only possible at a scheduled meeting or special session. The contract wording decides what counts (official announcement, signing, not reports).
stages.distribution: Feasible-set logic: the destination distribution is supported on a subset of teams; governance outcomes are gated binary events conditional on a meeting.

stages.name: Information flow from insiders to official announcements
stages.description: Public reports from league insiders arrive before official announcements and move beliefs, but their reliability varies by reporter and report type (pending talks versus agreed terms); the lag between the report and the official step determines how much of the hazard is realised inside the contract window. Rules requiring an official announcement make unconfirmed reports non-settling.
stages.distribution: Bayesian update with report-specific likelihood ratios; lag between report and announcement ranges from hours to months with heavy tails.

stages.name: Personal career and front-office decisions (retirement, GM hire)
stages.description: KXNHLRETIRE is a single person's decision before a deadline: the hazard rises with age, an expiring or expired contract, declining production or chronic injury, and falls with milestones still within reach and a signed contract year left; statements by player and agent are informative but only a qualifying announcement settles. KXNHLNEXTGM is a choice among a small candidate pool once a vacancy exists: internal assistant GMs, former GMs and executives tied to the club president or owner; the hire timing follows the search process, and insider reports of interviews and finalists move probabilities.
stages.distribution: Retirement is Bernoulli with a strongly age-dependent hazard that is concentrated in the off-season; the GM market is a categorical over a handful of named candidates plus a long 'other' tail, with timing mass after season end or a firing.

talent_strength.note: Only through the retirement contract: declining production lowers the value of continuing and raises the retirement hazard.

coaching_scheme.note: None of the contracts depend on on-ice tactics or coaching systems; the destination of a player can be influenced by a coach, but only as part of the news signal.

environment.note: Venue and travel conditions do not drive a transaction, an award or a governance decision; the only environmental factor is arena readiness for expansion, handled in the governance input.

game_context_script.note: No game state or score path affects these events, which resolve through institutional processes rather than within-game play.

pace_volume.note: There is no counting process of plays or shots behind these contracts; the only volume-like quantity is the number of calendar opportunities in the window, covered by the calendar input.

efficiency_conversion.note: No conversion rate (shooting, saving) settles these contracts; production only enters the Lindsay vote through the award model.

officiating_rules.note: No on-ice officiating applies; the rules that matter are the settlement text and league governance procedures, covered under the contract and governance inputs.

nhl.player_contract_status_clauses.label: Player contract status and movement clauses
nhl.player_contract_status_clauses.mechanism: Contract expiry year, cap hit, no-trade or no-move clauses, arbitration and free-agent status for the named player.
nhl.player_contract_status_clauses.rationale: Destination markets are bounded by the contract: a player under a long contract with a no-movement clause can only move with consent, while a player on an expiring contract becomes a free agent on a known date; the same inputs determine whether any team can acquire him at all.
nhl.player_contract_status_clauses.measurement: For the player compile from cap sites: contract end year, AAV, NMC/NTC status and no-trade list if public, RFA/UFA status and arbitration rights, extension eligibility date, and the signing/trade windows of the NHL calendar; compute months to free agency and an indicator of whether a trade requires consent; refresh weekly and after each transaction; encode a feasible destination set with ex ante constraint flags.
raw_data: player contracts with clauses and dates, league calendar
nhl.player_contract_status_clauses.why: Sets the support of the destination distribution and the timing of movement for the next-team contract.

nhl.suitor_cap_and_roster_fit.label: Suitor cap space and roster-fit table
nhl.suitor_cap_and_roster_fit.mechanism: Cap space, positional need and competitive window of each team relative to the player.
nhl.suitor_cap_and_roster_fit.rationale: A destination requires cap room and a lineup need; teams with space and a hole at the position are the likely suitors, and the number of feasible suitors changes the probabilities in a partition over 32 teams.
nhl.suitor_cap_and_roster_fit.measurement: For each team compute projected cap space at the next signing window (cap ceiling minus committed salary for the next season, adjusted for LTIR), roster need for the position (depth chart gap in impact score), and a competitive-window score (points percentage and age of core); form a suitor score = space feasibility x need x window with weights fit on past star free-agent decisions (5 seasons, k=15 events); normalise to a probability vector with the player's preference (location, prior team) if known.
raw_data: team cap tables, roster depth by position
nhl.suitor_cap_and_roster_fit.why: Provides the probability vector across teams that the contract's partition requires.

nhl.expansion_governance_gates.label: Expansion governance gates and readiness checklist
nhl.expansion_governance_gates.mechanism: Calendar of Board of Governors meetings and the readiness steps (ownership group, arena, fee, committee statements) for a candidate city.
nhl.expansion_governance_gates.rationale: An expansion award requires an official Board decision, which cannot occur without an expansion process and a meeting; the hazard of a decision before a given date is the probability that these gates are cleared in time.
nhl.expansion_governance_gates.measurement: Record the scheduled Board of Governors meeting dates before the market close, the public status of the expansion process (committee formed, applications requested, ownership group named, arena plan, expansion fee level) and commissioner statements with dates; assign a stage score (0-5) and map stage to the probability of a vote before the date using historical expansion cases (Vegas 2016, Seattle 2018, Utah transfer) with wide uncertainty; update after each public statement.
raw_data: dated governance statements, meeting calendar, bid status
nhl.expansion_governance_gates.why: Defines whether the formal decision step can occur inside the window, which dominates the probability for the expansion contract.

nhl.insider_report_credibility.label: Insider report credibility and lag
nhl.insider_report_credibility.mechanism: Reporter- and report-type-specific hit rate and lag between a report and the official announcement.
nhl.insider_report_credibility.rationale: Reports of talks, offers or agreements differ in reliability; the contract only settles on official actions, so the hit rate and lag set how much a report should move the probability within the time window.
nhl.insider_report_credibility.measurement: Collect reports by named insiders on transactions for 5 seasons with report type (talks, close, agreed, official), then label outcomes (official within 7, 30, 90 days); compute per-reporter and per-type hit rate with Beta(2,2) prior and the distribution of lag; convert to likelihood ratio of a report for the contract's event within its window; store report timestamp and wording.
free_sources: Public posts of NHL insiders (own capture)
raw_data: dated insider reports with type and later official outcomes
nhl.insider_report_credibility.why: Controls the weight to put on news in markets that settle only on official events.

nhl.reference_class_hazard.label: Class-specific event hazard (player move by contract class, expansion by process stage, award by finalist)
nhl.reference_class_hazard.mechanism: Each off-field contract belongs to a narrow reference class whose hazard is estimated separately: a player changing teams inside a dated window given contract status and team situation, an expansion announcement given its process stage, an award given its finalist set.
nhl.reference_class_hazard.rationale: The pooled base rate is meaningless for three unrelated generating processes. Narrow classes have small samples, so each hazard needs an explicit estimator and shrinkage, and expansion has so few events that its probability is a stage-transition judgement rather than a frequency.
nhl.reference_class_hazard.measurement: Player move: from NHL transactions since 2005-06, hazard of a trade or signing with a new team within the window = logistic regression on contract class (expiring, term remaining, NMC/NTC), month, team standing and cap space, shrunk to the class mean with k=30 player-windows; status quo probability = 1 minus the hazard. Expansion: stage-transition probabilities between process stages (committee formed, applications, ownership named, vote scheduled) from the 1991-2021 expansion waves (n of about 8), reported with wide intervals and never as a precise frequency. Award: conditional-logit winner-among-finalists from past finalist sets. As-of: latest transaction wire and governance statements; never a market price.
free_sources: NHL transactions pages and PuckPedia/CapWages contract tables
raw_data: player transaction history with contract status at the time
league expansion process timeline
award finalists and winners by season
nhl.reference_class_hazard.why: Replaces the audited-WEAK pooled base rate by per-class hazards so that rare-event markets have a defined central quantity.

nhl.retirement_hazard_profile.label: Veteran retirement hazard by age, contract status, production and health
nhl.retirement_hazard_profile.mechanism: The probability that a player announces an immediately effective retirement before a season start depends on age, contract status, recent production, injury history and remaining milestones.
nhl.retirement_hazard_profile.rationale: Retirement contracts are about one person, so the base rate must be conditioned on the right covariates; an unsigned 39-year-old with declining scoring is very different from a 39-year-old with a year left, and a farewell-season announcement does not count under the rules.
nhl.retirement_hazard_profile.measurement: Logistic hazard fit on all NHL skaters and goalies aged 33+ per off-season since 2005: outcome = retirement announced before next season start; covariates = age, contract years remaining (0/1/2+), points or GSAx per 60 trend over 2 seasons, games missed to injury last season, career milestone distance (e.g. goals to a record), unrestricted-free-agent status at July 1; apply to the named player with as-of date of the market; shrink player-specific adjustments toward the fitted rate.
free_sources: Hockey-Reference player pages and retirement lists
raw_data: player age, contract expiry, career stats by season
retirement announcement dates
injury games missed
nhl.retirement_hazard_profile.why: KXNHLRETIRE settles on a qualifying retirement announcement before the season start; this hazard is the input that generates it.

nhl.gm_candidate_pool.label: GM vacancy candidate pool and hiring-process stage
nhl.gm_candidate_pool.mechanism: Once a club's GM chair is vacant, the next GM is drawn from a small set of candidates whose probability depends on internal ties, prior GM experience, links to the club president/owner and reported interview stage.
nhl.gm_candidate_pool.rationale: The GM market is a categorical over named people, so the input must enumerate candidates and their stage; a generic hire base rate says nothing about who is hired, and reports of interviews and finalists are the main information events.
nhl.gm_candidate_pool.measurement: Per vacancy (as of the market timestamp): list candidates named in credible reports plus internal assistant GMs; score each with a multinomial logit fit on NHL GM hires since 2005 using features internal (0/1), prior NHL GM (0/1), shared employer history with the club president/owner (0/1), reported stage (none/interviewed/finalist/agreed); residual mass to 'other'; time-to-hire from vacancy date via empirical distribution of search lengths.
free_sources: Insider reports (TSN, Sportsnet, The Athletic) captured with timestamps
raw_data: GM hire history with dates, prior roles and links
candidate lists and interview reports with timestamps
nhl.gm_candidate_pool.why: KXNHLNEXTGM settles on which person is named GM of the club before the date; the candidate pool is the outcome space.

nhl.offfield_base_rate.reason: A single pooled base rate for destination, governance and award events is meaningless; each class needs its own narrow reference class and time-varying hazard. Replaced everywhere in this record by the class-specific nhl.reference_class_hazard (per-class estimators defined there).

nhl.announcement_calendar.reason: Fixed league dates (free agency, trade windows, Board meetings, award ceremonies) concentrate the hazard and bound feasible dates.

nhl.news.reason: Insider reporting is the main information channel, but unstructured news needs a credibility and lag model to be usable.

m.rules_text.reason: Settlement requires official announcements and defines what counts as the next team, tie payoffs and retirement outcomes.

m.quote_history.reason: Price reaction after reports measures the market's reading of news and is the quantity to be compared, not a causal input.

m.volume_oi.reason: Volume and open interest describe the market's liquidity; they say nothing about whether the event will occur.

m.lifecycle.reason: Close time and open date set how much of the hazard lies inside the window; a rule-derived settlement and window parameter, not a driver of the outcome, hence secondary.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook or exchange prices on these events, if they exist, are benchmarks and must not be features for a fundamentals model.

m.strike_hit_rates.reason: Historical settled frequencies on Kalshi for these novelty contracts are tiny samples and are outcomes of the market itself, not causes.

nhl.award_vote_share_model.reason: Served only KXNHLLINDSAY, which the final series assignment moved to season_awards_and_stats (stage s5 there); transactions and expansion do not resolve by vote.

nhl.player_season_points_projection.reason: Production projection was a proxy for Lindsay votes; with Lindsay reassigned, neither the next-team nor the expansion contract depends on a player's season points.

interactions.mechanism: Hazard is concentrated at calendar points (free agency opening, trade windows, Board meetings), so the probability of an event inside a window is the sum of mass at the dated gates inside it, not a constant hazard times duration.
interactions.how_to_test: Build the calendar of gate dates inside the window and compare realised event timing over past seasons with a constant-hazard model.

interactions.mechanism: A report of an agreement raises probability, but the contract settles only on an official step and a lag between the two, so the effect depends on the credibility of the source and on whether the official step falls before the contract closes.
interactions.how_to_test: Label past reports by type and measure the share followed by the official action within the window length.

interactions.mechanism: A destination needs both a feasible contract status (consent, expiry, window) and a suitor with space and need; the probability for a team is the product of feasibility and fit, so a team with ideal fit but a closed window has nearly zero probability.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised destinations with the product of feasibility and fit scores versus fit alone over past star moves.

interactions.mechanism: Expansion before the deadline requires an expansion process to have reached a Board vote; unless a meeting with the vote is scheduled inside the window the probability is near zero, a threshold on the governance stage rather than a gradual hazard.
interactions.how_to_test: Record the stage of past expansion bids at each month before announcement and compare with the time to the Board vote.

interactions.mechanism: An expired contract without an offer turns a moderate age hazard into a high one, whereas a signed final year keeps a veteran playing almost regardless of age; the retirement probability jumps at the contract-expiry state rather than rising smoothly with age.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the retirement hazard with and without an age x contract-years interaction on 33+ players since 2005 and compare log loss.

nonlinearities.shape: Spiked hazard at dated gates
nonlinearities.why: Free agency opening and trade deadlines produce a very high short-term hazard compared with the remainder of the window, so the probability of a change of team is a step function of calendar position, not linear in time.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in proximity to contract expiry
nonlinearities.why: The probability a player moves rises sharply in the final contract year and at the free-agency date; years remaining is a convex, non-linear predictor, and clauses create hard zeros for non-consenting destinations.

nonlinearities.shape: Logistic in report type and source reliability
nonlinearities.why: A report of agreed terms from a reliable source moves the probability close to one while a report of talks barely moves it; the map from report to probability is sigmoid in a credibility score.

contract.settlement_definition: Player season counting contracts resolved on official 2026-27 regular-season statistics: KXNHLPSEASONGOALS and KXNHLSEASONGOALS pay YES if the named player scores at least the stated number of goals (e.g. 60 or 40) during the regular season; KXNHLSEASONPPTS (reassigned here from the single-game points archetype) pays YES if the player reaches the stated points total, points being goals plus assists, regular season only. No minimum-games, trade or retirement clause is stated. The two goal series have empty secondary rules; only KXNHLSEASONPPTS states 'regular season stats only'.

rules_evidence.quote: If Macklin Celebrini scores at least 60 goals during the 2026-27 NHL regular season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: A season goal total threshold with a floor_strike of 59.5; the quantity is games played times goal rate, and no game-played minimum or trade clause is stated.

rules_evidence.quote: If Brady Tkachuk scores at least 40 goals during the 2026-27 NHL regular season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: A second goal-total series with the same 'at least N' construction at a lower threshold; only regular-season goals count and no games-played condition is stated.

rules_evidence.quote: Points = Goals + Assists. This market refers to regular season stats only.
rules_evidence.establishes: Season points are goals plus assists over the regular season only, so assist credit (IPP, on-ice goals for) enters, and playoff points are excluded.

variants_and_edge_cases: Two goal series (KXNHLPSEASONGOALS, KXNHLSEASONGOALS) price the same quantity with different thresholds and should be consistent for a player listed in both; points (KXNHLSEASONPPTS) add assists, which have a different persistence from goals.

Player goal totals: the official goals statistic counts empty-net and overtime goals but shootout-deciding goals are not credited to players (sc4); a traded player keeps his total; no minimum games clause is stated, so injury only lowers the total.
Strike construction: 'at least N' with floor_strike N-0.5; a player sitting exactly on the threshold at season end resolves YES, so late-season pace matters at the margin.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official NHL regular-season player statistics (goals, assists, points).

mechanism.summary: Player season counting contracts are sums over a fixed schedule, so the outcome is a rate times opportunities with uncertainty in both. For a player's goal total the rate is shots per game times shooting percentage, each with a talent component and a luck component; for points the rate adds assist credit on team goals while he is on the ice. The opportunities are games played (zero-inflated by injuries and rest) and minutes (role, power-play share), and the league scoring environment shifts everyone at once. Early in the season the to-date total is only a small piece of the total, so the talent prior and the age trajectory dominate, and the threshold probability is the upper tail of a compound count with random rate and random games.

stages.name: Talent prior and rate decomposition for the player
stages.description: A player's goal rate per game equals shot volume per game times shooting percentage. Shot volume is the most stable component and is anchored by shot rate per 60 and ice time; shooting percentage regresses strongly toward a player-specific talent estimate built from xG per shot. Age curves shift both and early-season data are weighted lightly. This stage produces the rate distribution for the rest of the season, not a point estimate.
stages.distribution: Rate distribution with posterior sd of order 10-15 percent of the mean for established scorers; shooting percentage has a binomial noise component of order sd 2.5-3 points over a season.

stages.name: Opportunity: games played, minutes and power-play role
stages.description: The number of games played is capped at 82 and reduced by injury and rest; for a star, the distribution has most mass at 78-82 and a long left tail from injuries. Minutes and PP unit role set the volume per game, and PP1 membership is more persistent than even-strength points. A player on a high-scoring PP unit has a rate floor that survives regression. These opportunities convert linearly into goals once the rate is fixed.
stages.distribution: Games played: 82 minus a zero-inflated heavy-tailed missed-games count (about 10-15 percent chance of missing 15+ games for veterans).

stages.name: Accumulation, to-date information and thresholds
stages.description: The season total is goals to date plus a rest-of-season sum; with about 68 games remaining the remaining sum is a compound count with random rate and random games. A threshold such as 60 goals (floor 59.5) requires a rate near 0.75 per game over 80 games; the probability is a steep function of the mean because the Poisson sd at a mean near 60 is already about 7.7 goals and the random scoring rate and games played raise the total sd to roughly 9-12 goals, so the curve is less steep than a pure Poisson implies (the exact sd must be fitted). The league scoring environment also moves the mean for all players together.
stages.distribution: Season goals ~ negative binomial or compound Poisson with mean mu and sd about sqrt(mu) times 1.2 plus rate and games uncertainty; P(>=60) rises smoothly with mu over a wide range (a total sd near 9-12 goals, to be fitted rather than assumed).

stages.name: Settlement mapping and ties
stages.description: Resolution uses official counts: goals and assists credited to the skater (shootout-deciding goals are not credited to players), regular season only. The strike construction (floor 59.5 meaning 'at least 60', points thresholds inclusive) creates positive mass exactly at the boundary, and post-game scoring changes (assist corrections) can move a total by one late in the season.
stages.distribution: Discrete thresholds on integer counts; dead-heat 1/N payouts on ties; boundary events have positive probability mass.

stages.name: Player season points chain (KXNHLSEASONPPTS)
stages.description: A season points threshold such as 110+ for a defenceman is points banked plus a sum over remaining games of the per-game point process: on-ice goals for per 60, state-specific time on ice (especially power-play share), individual points percentage (credit on team goals), then the games-played distribution. Defencemen at 110 points sit in the extreme right tail of the rate posterior and depend on PP1 role security and health.
stages.distribution: Compound sum: negative-binomial per-game points over a games-played pmf with an injury left tail; the threshold probability lives in the right tail of the rate posterior for rare scorers.

opponent_matchup.note: A player's season total integrates over roughly 68 remaining opponents, so opponent quality averages out to a small common shift absorbed by the league scoring environment; no matchup-level mechanism is needed for goal or point thresholds.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and load management reach a player's season total only through games played, modelled by the games-played hazard; standings stakes change star usage only in the last weeks and are not a separate driver here.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching systems affect a player's season total only through ice time, PP unit and linemates, which are modelled as role inputs; team-level contracts are driven by ratings that already include coaching effects.

game_context_script.note: Single-game script (score effects, empty-net timing) averages out across 82 games and enters season counts only through small average effects on rates; no game-level mechanism is needed for season totals.

officiating_rules.note: Penalty-calling tendencies affect season power-play opportunities, but their season-level effect is absorbed in the league scoring environment and team PP share, so no separate officiating input is needed.

nhl.games_played_hazard.label: Games-played hazard (injury, rest and load management)
nhl.games_played_hazard.mechanism: Distribution of games missed for a player over the season given age, position, injury history and team situation.
nhl.games_played_hazard.rationale: A season total is capped by games played; a 60-goal pace needs about 78-82 games, so the left tail from injuries is the main downside. A distribution (not an expected value) is needed because missing a month removes the contract's chances.
nhl.games_played_hazard.measurement: From 10 seasons of player-game logs compute for each skater-season games missed, then fit a zero-inflated negative binomial for games missed with covariates age, position, prior-season games missed (weights 0.5/0.3/0.2), prior major injury count, and current injury status; update for the current season with games already played and the current injury report; shrink toward position-age cohort with k=25 player-seasons; output the pmf of games remaining played given status.
free_sources: Man Games Lost datasets (paid) or injury trackers
raw_data: player-season games played, injury reports with dates, ages
nhl.games_played_hazard.why: Opportunity cap for all player season counting contracts, and the source of the left tail of the goal total.

nhl.league_scoring_environment.label: League scoring environment drift
nhl.league_scoring_environment.mechanism: Current-season league goals per game relative to the prior-season baseline, with shrinkage.
nhl.league_scoring_environment.rationale: League scoring levels shift between seasons by a few percent (rules, enforcement, goalie equipment, shot quality), moving every player's goal expectation together; a 60-goal threshold is sensitive to a three percent level change.
nhl.league_scoring_environment.measurement: Compute league goals per team per game and PP opportunities per game to date; the season-end estimate is a precision-weighted average of the prior-season value (weight 0.6) and the to-date value with game-count weight n/(n+250); report the estimated multiplier and its sd (about 1.5 percent) and apply it as a common factor on all player and team scoring rates in simulation; refresh weekly.
raw_data: league-wide goals, games and PP counts by season and date
nhl.league_scoring_environment.why: Common scale factor for season goals; failing to model it overstates certainty across all player thresholds.

nhl.player_season_points_projection.label: Player season points projection (rate x games-played distribution)
nhl.player_season_points_projection.mechanism: A season points threshold is reached by points already banked plus per-game production on the games still to be played, so the outcome is the sum of a rate (role, time on ice, power-play share, on-ice chance creation and credit share) and an opportunity count (games played).
nhl.player_season_points_projection.rationale: Season-points contracts such as a 110+ points threshold for a defenceman sit in the extreme tail of a rate times games distribution, so both the central rate and its dispersion matter. Rate comes from the same components as the single-game record (role, power-play time, on-ice xGF, individual points percentage); games remaining comes from the games-played hazard. The subtle part is that role changes (power-play unit, line, injuries to teammates) move the rate level for the rest of the season.
nhl.player_season_points_projection.measurement: Points to date P0 plus the sum over remaining games g of expected points per game, where per-game expected points = sum over strength states of (on-ice goals-for per 60 x projected state time on ice per 60 x individual points percentage in that state), using 3 seasons weighted 0.5/0.3/0.2 with half-life 1.5 seasons, shrunk to position-and-role priors (k=25 on-ice goals) and updated for the current season by a gamma-Poisson rate posterior; multiply by the pmf of games remaining from nhl.games_played_hazard; simulate 20000 seasons with negative-binomial per-game dispersion fitted on player-seasons of comparable rate; report P(total >= threshold). As-of: all games before the contract date, with the current power-play unit and line assignment from the latest lineup report.
free_sources: NHL API player game logs and play-by-play (api-web.nhle.com)
raw_data: player-game goals, assists, time on ice by strength state
on-ice goals-for per strength state
games-played and injury history per player-season
nhl.player_season_points_projection.why: Gives the season-points contracts a market-free chain (rate, role, games played) instead of leaving them to a single-game or goals-only mechanism.

nhl.stat_dist.reason: The distribution of season totals (compound count with random rate and games) decides threshold probabilities; the draft's per-game framing must be aggregated with rate uncertainty.

nhl.toi.reason: Season-long ice time projection (especially PP) scales the rate; per-game TOI must be a distribution over the remaining season, not a current value.

nhl.pp_role.reason: A PP1 slot gives a persistent rate floor; the main quantity is whether the role is secure for the season.

nhl.ixg_player.reason: Most stable estimate of goal-scoring talent for the rate; used with shrinkage because finishing is noisy.

nhl.finishing.reason: Persistent shooting talent is small relative to season noise; the shrinkage constant is the key property.

nhl.lines.reason: Line combinations change frequently over a season, so current lines carry little information for a season total beyond the role and linemate quality captured elsewhere.

nhl.linemate_quality.reason: Linemate effects are unstable over a season and partially captured by on-ice rates and PP role; evidence of persistence is weak.

nhl.career_trajectory.reason: Mislabelled secondary: with only a dozen games played the age curve and rookie/sophomore ramp are the main prior for the rest of the season.

nhl.shot_rate.reason: Mislabelled secondary: shot volume is the most stable component of goal scoring and anchors the projection, with finishing layered on top.

nhl.team_season_points_distribution.reason: Team points layer served the team series, which the final series assignment moved to season_futures (definition now carried there); no player counting contract needs it.

nhl.schedule_sequence_profile.reason: Schedule-path driver for team streak and division contracts, now in season_futures; a player's season total depends on games played and rate, not on the order of opponents.

nhl.win_streak_extremum_dist.reason: Only KXNHLWSTREAK used it, and that series was reassigned to season_futures (carried there); irrelevant to player goal and point totals.

nhl.loser_point_rate.reason: Loser points matter for team standings contracts, which moved to season_futures; no player counting contract depends on extra-time loss points.

nhl.rating_posterior_uncertainty.reason: Team rating uncertainty drove the team series now in season_futures; player rate uncertainty is carried by the player projections' own posteriors.

interactions.mechanism: A season goal total equals games played times goals per game, so uncertainty in games and in rate multiply; a 60-goal pace needs both near-full health and a high rate, so the threshold probability is much lower than the product of marginal 'pace' and 'health' intuitions.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute P(>=60) by simulation with and without games-played variability and compare with a fixed-82-game model.

interactions.mechanism: To-date goals above expected regress toward the xG-based talent, and the amount of regression depends on shots taken so far: with about 40 shots to date the prior should dominate and the to-date shooting percentage should be almost ignored.
interactions.how_to_test: Test predictive weight on to-date shooting percentage as a function of shots taken in rolling seasons.

interactions.mechanism: The league scoring multiplier applies to all players simultaneously, so thresholds on goals for different stars move together; this makes cross-player outcomes positively correlated and a common-factor error mis-prices all goal ladders in the same direction.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate year-to-year league scoring change and compare with cross-player residual correlation in goals.

interactions.mechanism: For an extreme points target (e.g. 110 for a defenceman) the required rate is near the top of the posterior, so even a two-week absence or a demotion from PP1 pushes the needed rest-of-season pace beyond plausible values; the probability drops in a step once games missed or role loss crosses that point rather than declining smoothly.
interactions.how_to_test: In historical player-seasons, compare threshold attainment for top-decile scorers by games missed bucket and PP1 continuity against a model linear in games missed.

interactions.mechanism: Goals and points for the same player share the goal-scoring rate and the league factor, so the two contracts on one player are strongly dependent; assists add a second, less persistent component whose regression toward on-ice expectation is faster than for goals, so points thresholds regress more than goal thresholds after a hot start.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare split-half reliability of goals per game and assists per game across player-seasons, and the correlation of goal and point threshold outcomes for the same players.

interactions.mechanism: Age affects goals first through ice time and PP role (a regime change when a player loses PP1) before it affects shooting rate; the response is a regime switch at the role change, not a smooth decline.
interactions.how_to_test: Track PP1 membership by age and compare goal rate changes before and after loss of PP1.

nonlinearities.shape: S-curve near the threshold, flatter than Poisson
nonlinearities.why: The probability of reaching the threshold is a logistic-like function of the expected total whose slope is set by the total sd (Poisson about 7.7 near 60 goals, roughly 9-12 once random rate and games played are included, to be fitted), so a model's mean error of a few goals is still a large probability error near the strike.

nonlinearities.shape: Truncated at 82 with a heavy left tail
nonlinearities.why: Games played cannot exceed 82 and the downside from injuries is a long tail; the expected value understates the cost, and the contract probability depends on the full distribution, not its mean.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in the rate posterior's right tail for extreme targets
nonlinearities.why: For rare totals such as 110 points the YES probability lives in the right tail of the rate posterior, so it rises convexly with the posterior sd; underestimating rate uncertainty prices these contracts far too low.
